citations.quote:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), read with the state
space vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited tensor construction.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator
$$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the
state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector
preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration. When a sector preparation is paired with an operator or a
spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*$, where $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow
H^{\otimes n}$ is the isometric inclusion and $j^*$ is the orthogonal
projection viewed as a map into the sector. This extension is a density
operator on the labelled space: by clause (a) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
$\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ in trace norm for an orthonormal family in the
sector and nonnegative weights summing to one. The family $(ju_k)$ is
orthonormal in the labelled space, so the same clause gives the density
$\sum_kw_kT_{ju_k,ju_k}$ there; its action is $j\rho j^*$, since both agree on
the sector and vanish on its orthogonal complement. If the sector is zero,
there is no density preparation of trace one and this convention is vacuous.

**(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space
$H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the
declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,
$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\bigl(D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\bigr)\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$
in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$
with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and
$x$ in the sector satisfy $\langle Ay,x\rangle=\langle y,Ax\rangle=0$,
so the complement is invariant as well; splitting each vector into its two
orthogonal components gives $AP_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}A$. For an arbitrary
bounded operator, invariance alone need not preserve the complement and is
not asserted equivalent to commutation. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary with which the
framework reads the adopted P6 assumptions: they add no assumption to P1 and
P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector
readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of
this definition. The definition asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no
dynamics, no measurement instrument and no empirical fact; whether a
laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}\in H$ write $v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1}\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=v_{\pi^{-1}(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n-1)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}$ have a repeated factor, that is, $v_i=v_j$ for some distinct $i,j\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, then $P_-(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=0$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $n\ge1$, let $H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold
completed tensor power with $H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$, let $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
be the permutation unitaries and let
$P_\sigma^{(n)}$, $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, be the sector projections
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), with sector space
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq H^{\otimes n}.$$
For $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
be the operator of clause (a) below, and put
$$\Sigma(O):=\sum_{i=1}^n O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n}).$$
Identify $H^{\otimes n}$ with $H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$ by the
surjective linear isometry $J_n$ of clause (b) below, and let
$\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}$ be the partial trace of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-finite-partial-trace-and-schmidt]] clause (a) over the
second factor of that identification. Then:

(a) *slot operators*: for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and every
$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ there is a unique $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
with $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{i-1}\otimes Ov_i\otimes v_{i+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$
for all $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$; it satisfies $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$ and
$(O^*)^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$; in particular $O=O^*$ gives $O^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$;

(b) *parenthesisation*: the assignment
$v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\mapsto v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$
extends to a surjective linear isometry
$J_n:H^{\otimes n}\to H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$; for $n=1$ the
empty product is $1\in\mathbb C$ and $J_1u=u\otimes1$;

(c) *permutation invariance*: $U_\pi\,\Sigma(O)\,U_\pi^*=\Sigma(O)$ for every
$\pi\in S_n$; consequently $\Sigma(O)$ preserves both sector spaces and commutes with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$:
$$\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)};$$

(d) *trace law*: for every density operator $\rho$ on the sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]
clause (a)), let $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow H^{\otimes n}$ be
the isometric inclusion and define its zero extension
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$; then
for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=n\,\operatorname{tr}(\gamma\,O)$,
where $\gamma:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}\bigl(J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}\bigr)\in\mathcal B(H)$;

(e) *the reduced operator is a density operator*: the operator $\gamma$ of
clause (d) is a density operator on $H$; it is independent of the choice of
slot in the sense that it equals the partial trace of $\widetilde\rho$ over
the other $n-1$ slots in the parenthesisation in which the retained slot is
the one the display names; for $n=1$, $\gamma=\rho$. If
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\{0\}$, there is no density operator of trace one on
that sector, so clauses (d)-(e) make no assertion about a sector preparation;

(f) *scope*: clauses (a)-(e) are exact operator identities on the
finite-dimensional labelled tensor powers; no physical system, particle
species, preparation or measurement is asserted, and the parameter $n$ is a
dimension count of the construction, not an observed particle number.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

For every natural $n$, the map
$\operatorname{tr}:M_n(F)\to F$ is linear:

$$\operatorname{tr}(A+B)=\operatorname{tr}(A)+\operatorname{tr}(B),\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\lambda A)=\lambda\operatorname{tr}(A).$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
real or complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let
$T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class ([[def-trace-class-operator]]) and let
$S\in\mathcal B(H)$ be bounded. Then $ST$ and $TS$ are trace class and
$$\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\operatorname{tr}(TS) .$$
If $A,B\in\mathcal B(H)$ are Hilbert–Schmidt relative to a supplied Hilbert
basis $E$ of $H$ ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), then the products $AB$ and
$BA$ are trace class and
$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric
projections $P_\pm^{(n)}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]). Then:

(a) *Slater vectors*: for $n\ge2$ and orthonormal $u_1,\dots,u_n\in H$, the
Slater vector
$$S(u_1,\dots,u_n):=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\,u_{\widehat{\sigma}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{\widehat{\sigma}(n)}$$
satisfies $\|S(u_1,\dots,u_n)\|=1$ and
$S(u_1,\dots,u_n)=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)$;

(b) *exclusion*: if $u_i=u_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then
$P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)=0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] (d));

(c) *two orbitals, bounded pair interaction*: let $u,v\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
be normalized and orthogonal, let $W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and
bounded with $W(-z)=W(z)$ for a.e. $z$, let
$\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3)\to L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ be the
Euclidean product unitary
([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]), put
$\varphi_\pm:=(u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u)/\sqrt2$ and
$$D:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}|u(x)|^2|v(y)|^2W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,\qquad X:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}\,W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,$$
integrals of absolutely integrable functions. Then $D,X\in\mathbb R$ and the
pair expectation of the multiplier $M_W$ in the two spatial states is
$$\bigl\langle M_W(\Theta\varphi_\pm),\Theta\varphi_\pm\bigr\rangle=D\pm X .$$

(d) *repulsive Coulomb exchange*: let $\kappa>0$, $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$, let
$u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\cap L^2$ be normalized and orthogonal
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
The vectors $\Theta\varphi_\pm$ belong to $D(M_W)$: Hardy translated in the $y$ variable and Tonelli give $\iint|u(x)v(y)|^2/|x-y|^2\le4\|u\|_2^2\|\nabla v\|_2^2<\infty$, and the swapped product has the same property. Then the integrals $D$ and $X$ converge absolutely, $0\le D<\infty$,
$X\in\mathbb R$ with $X\ge0$; consequently
$D-X\le D+X$, i.e. the antisymmetric spatial pair state has the lower
expectation of the repulsive Coulomb pair interaction.

The exchange calculation is a statement about the indicated spatial vectors; it
does not deduce the spin-statistics assignment of any species, and combining the
spatial states with spin requires a separately stipulated symmetry rule. No
physical interpretation of $D$, $X$ or the states is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}\in H$ write $v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1}\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=v_{\pi^{-1}(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n-1)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}$ have a repeated factor, that is, $v_i=v_j$ for some distinct $i,j\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, then $P_-(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=0$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

derivations.claim: [The readout is a bounded self-adjoint sector observable] By [F2] each slot operator is bounded with $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$, so $\Sigma(O)$ is bounded with $\|\Sigma(O)\|\le N\|O\|$; since $O=O^*$, [F2] gives $O^{(i)*}=O^{(i)}$ for every $i$ and $\Sigma(O)^*=\Sigma(O)$. By [F2] $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$, hence preserves $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ and its orthogonal complement, and the restriction $A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator on the sector space; with the unit $u_O$ the pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is therefore an assigned sharp observable in the sense of [F3].

[Reduced preparation of product-type states] Let $u_1,\dots,u_N$ be pairwise orthonormal, put $x:=u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N$ and let $\Psi$ be the unit vector of clause (c) for $\sigma=-$ or $\sigma=+$; both satisfy $P_\sigma^{(N)}\Psi=\Psi$ by [F4], and both equal $\sqrt{N!}\,P_\sigma^{(N)}x$. Since $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ and $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is self-adjoint, $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=N!\langle\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,P_\sigma^{(N)}x\rangle=N!\langle P_\sigma^{(N)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,x\rangle=N!\cdot\frac1{N!}\sum_{\tau\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\tau)\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle$, with $\operatorname{sgn}_+=1$ and $\operatorname{sgn}_-=\operatorname{sgn}$. For fixed $\tau$, $\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\langle Ou_{\widehat{\tau}^{-1}(i)},u_i\rangle\prod_{k\ne i}\langle u_{\widehat{\tau}^{-1}(k)},u_k\rangle$ by [F1] and the elementary-tensor pairing, and orthonormality makes every factor $\delta_{\widehat{\tau}^{-1}(k),k}$ vanish unless $\tau=\mathrm{id}$; hence only the identity permutation contributes and $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\langle Ou_i,u_i\rangle$.

[The mean law] Let $\rho$ be a declared sector preparation with zero extension $\widetilde\rho$ and let $A_O$ be the readout of step 1.1. Since $A_O$ is bounded, [F3] gives $m_\rho(A_O)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A_O)$, and by steps 1.1 and [F2], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A_O)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. This proves (a) and (b).

[Product-type means and the reduced preparation] In the situation of step 1.2, the mean is $m_\rho(A_O)=\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle$, while the mean law of step 2.1 gives $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. The identity extends from self-adjoint $O$ to every $O$ by writing $O=(O+O^*)/2+i(O-O^*)/(2i)$ and using linearity of both pairings. Testing it against $O=T_{u,v}$ and using [F5], $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho T_{u,v})=\langle\gamma_\rho u,v\rangle$ and $N^{-1}\sum_j\langle T_{u,v}u_j,u_j\rangle=N^{-1}\sum_j\langle u_j,v\rangle\langle u,u_j\rangle$; the identity for all $u,v$ therefore gives $\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$, since two endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional space with equal pairings against every rank-one operator are equal. This proves (c).

[Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1-2.1 prove (a) and (b) and step 3.1 proves (c). Every quantity is a spectral datum of the declared finite-mode sector model and the argument used only P1, P2, P6 and the finite-dimensional tensor and trace calculus; no measured mean, individual-particle property, separability statement or spatial reduction entered, which is (d).

citations.quote:
**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $N,r\ge1$ be integers, $H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r)$, $\mathcal S_N=(\mathbb C^r)^{\otimes N}$, and $M=r^N$. In the product basis $e_a=e_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{a_N}$ indexed by $a\in\{1,\dots,r\}^N$, identify $\mathcal S_N$ with $\mathbb C^M$ and write $\mathcal L_N=L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$. Then:

(a) There is a unique unitary $\Theta_N:H^{\otimes N}\to\mathcal L_N$ such that
$$[\Theta_N(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_N)]_a(x_1,\dots,x_N)=\prod_{j=1}^N[f_j(x_j)]_{a_j}.$$

(b) For $\pi\in S_N$, let $U_\pi$ be the permutation of the complete one-particle factors and $R_\pi e_a=e_{a_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{a_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(N)}}$ the permutation of spin factors. With $X^\pi=(x_{\widehat{\pi}(1)},\dots,x_{\widehat{\pi}(N)})$, the conjugate permutation is
$$\mathcal U_\pi:=\Theta_NU_\pi\Theta_N^{-1},\qquad (\mathcal U_\pi\Psi)(X)=R_\pi\Psi(X^\pi).$$
In particular $[\mathcal U_\pi\Psi]_a(X)=\Psi_{(a_{\widehat{\pi}(1)},\dots,a_{\widehat{\pi}(N)})}(X^\pi)$; averaging this combined action gives $\mathcal P_\pm=\Theta_NP_\pm^{(N)}\Theta_N^{-1}$.

(c) The component domain $\mathcal D_N=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$ is the set of tuples with every scalar component in $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$. If a scalar self-adjoint $T$ has this scalar domain and its domain is preserved by every spatial block permutation, commuting with that permutation on the domain, its finite direct sum $T_M\Psi=(T\Psi_a)_a$ on $\mathcal D_N$ is self-adjoint, retains every scalar lower bound $T\ge cI$, and commutes with the combined permutations on that domain. The restrictions of $T_M$ to $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\pm$, with domain $\mathcal D_N\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\pm$, are self-adjoint when the sector is nonzero; on the zero sector the unique zero operator has domain $\{0\}$.

(d) For matrices $A_j\in\mathcal B(\mathbb C^r)$, the constant spin action $A_1\otimes\cdots\otimes A_N$ preserves $\mathcal D_N$ and commutes with $T_M$. Its permutation covariance is
$$R_\pi(A_1\otimes\cdots\otimes A_N)R_\pi^{-1}=A_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes A_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(N)}.$$
Thus a common internal unitary $A^{\otimes N}$ commutes with $\mathcal U_\pi$, preserves both sectors and commutes with their restricted operators. This is a tensor identity and asserts no physical spin-statistics assignment. For $r=1$ all spin actions are scalar and $\Theta_N$ is the iterated scalar product unitary; for $N=1$ it is the identity component identification.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}\in H$ write $v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1}\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=v_{\pi^{-1}(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n-1)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}$ have a repeated factor, that is, $v_i=v_j$ for some distinct $i,j\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, then $P_-(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=0$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), let $a,b\ge1$, and let $\lambda_n$ denote Lebesgue measure on $\mathcal L(\mathbb R^n)$ as defined in [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]] and completed from Borel measure as in [[cor-lebesgue-sigma-algebra-is-the-completion-of-borel-lebesgue-measure]]. The product measure $\lambda_a\times\lambda_b$ exists by [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]], and under $\mathbb R^{a+b}=\mathbb R^a\times\mathbb R^b$, $\lambda_{a+b}$ is its completion ([[thm-euclidean-lebesgue-measure-is-the-completion-of-the-product-of-lebesgue-measures]]). Write $H_a=L^2(\mathbb R^a,\lambda_a)$ and $H_b=L^2(\mathbb R^b,\lambda_b)$, with $L^2$ understood as the almost-everywhere quotient of square-integrable measurable functions ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). Then there is a unique linear isometry

$$\Theta:H_a\widehat\otimes H_b\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^{a+b})$$

with $\Theta(f\otimes g)(x,y)=f(x)g(y)$ for all $f\in H_a$, $g\in H_b$ and a.e. $(x,y)$, and $\Theta$ is onto: it is a surjective linear isometry, hence unitary. Vector-valued or spin factors follow by finite component sums. No identification of non-Euclidean product measures is asserted.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to \mathbb C$ belong to
$L^1(\mu \times \nu)$. Then:

1. for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the section $f_x$ belongs to $L^1(\nu)$;
2. for $\nu$-almost every $y$, the section $f^y$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$;
3. after assigning the value $0$ on the exceptional parameter sets, the
   section-integral functions are integrable; and
4. the three integrals agree:
$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric
projections $P_\pm^{(n)}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]). Then:

(a) *Slater vectors*: for $n\ge2$ and orthonormal $u_1,\dots,u_n\in H$, the
Slater vector
$$S(u_1,\dots,u_n):=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\,u_{\widehat{\sigma}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{\widehat{\sigma}(n)}$$
satisfies $\|S(u_1,\dots,u_n)\|=1$ and
$S(u_1,\dots,u_n)=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)$;

(b) *exclusion*: if $u_i=u_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then
$P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)=0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] (d));

(c) *two orbitals, bounded pair interaction*: let $u,v\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
be normalized and orthogonal, let $W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and
bounded with $W(-z)=W(z)$ for a.e. $z$, let
$\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3)\to L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ be the
Euclidean product unitary
([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]), put
$\varphi_\pm:=(u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u)/\sqrt2$ and
$$D:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}|u(x)|^2|v(y)|^2W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,\qquad X:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}\,W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,$$
integrals of absolutely integrable functions. Then $D,X\in\mathbb R$ and the
pair expectation of the multiplier $M_W$ in the two spatial states is
$$\bigl\langle M_W(\Theta\varphi_\pm),\Theta\varphi_\pm\bigr\rangle=D\pm X .$$

(d) *repulsive Coulomb exchange*: let $\kappa>0$, $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$, let
$u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\cap L^2$ be normalized and orthogonal
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
The vectors $\Theta\varphi_\pm$ belong to $D(M_W)$: Hardy translated in the $y$ variable and Tonelli give $\iint|u(x)v(y)|^2/|x-y|^2\le4\|u\|_2^2\|\nabla v\|_2^2<\infty$, and the swapped product has the same property. Then the integrals $D$ and $X$ converge absolutely, $0\le D<\infty$,
$X\in\mathbb R$ with $X\ge0$; consequently
$D-X\le D+X$, i.e. the antisymmetric spatial pair state has the lower
expectation of the repulsive Coulomb pair interaction.

The exchange calculation is a statement about the indicated spatial vectors; it
does not deduce the spin-statistics assignment of any species, and combining the
spatial states with spin requires a separately stipulated symmetry rule. No
physical interpretation of $D$, $X$ or the states is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix integers $N,M\ge1$, $a>0$, and a real measurable function $V:\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R$ with $v=\operatorname{ess\,sup}|V|<\infty$. Put
$$\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),\qquad Y=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)=H^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),$$
where the vector space, pairing and Sobolev norm are the finite component sums of the scalar conventions of [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. Use the componentwise Plancherel unitary of [[thm-plancherel]], with the negative-sign $2\pi$ convention of [[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]]. Define
$$w(\xi)=4\pi^2a|\xi|^2,\qquad K=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_w\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(K)=\{u:w\mathcal F_2u\in\mathcal H\}.$$
Then $D(K)=Y$, and $Ku=-a\Delta u$ for every $u\in Y$, with the distributional Laplacian acting componentwise. The operator
$$H=K+M_V=-a\Delta+V,\qquad D(H)=Y,$$
is densely defined and self-adjoint on exactly $Y$, and $H\ge-v$. Both $K$ and $H$ have graph norms equivalent to the stated Sobolev norm, and $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$ is a core for both. For $z=\pm i\mu$ with $\mu>v$, there is the concrete two-sided inverse
$$R_H(z)=(H-z)^{-1}=R_0(z)\sum_{k\ge0}(-M_VR_0(z))^k,\qquad R_0(z)=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_{(w-z)^{-1}}\mathcal F_2,$$
with range exactly $Y$ and $\|R_H(z)\|\le(\mu-v)^{-1}$.

This realizes the equal-mass bounded spatial operator used at fixed $N$ by setting $a=\hbar^2/(2m)$ and any finite spin multiplicity $M$; for an $N$-fold spin-$s$ tensor the full multiplicity is $M=(2s+1)^N$. The lemma makes no statement about Coulomb potentials, unequal-mass operators, thermodynamic limits, or physical assignments. It uses no Axiom of Choice or Kato–Rellich theorem.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $N\ge1$ and $r\ge1$,
let $m_1,\dots,m_N>0$, $\hbar>0$, let $a_1,\dots,a_M\in\mathbb R^3$ be fixed
points, and let $z_{im},z_{ij}\in\mathbb R$ be real coefficients
($1\le i\le N$, $1\le m\le M$, $1\le i<j\le N$). Let $K$ be the free kinetic
operator of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]],
$D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$ with equivalent graph norm, and define
the singular multiplier
$$V(X):=\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{m=1}^M\frac{z_{im}}{|x_i-a_m|}+\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\frac{z_{ij}}{|x_i-x_j|},\qquad X=(x_1,\dots,x_N)\in\mathbb R^{3N},$$
as an a.e.-defined real measurable function
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). Then:

(a) each of the multipliers $u\mapsto u/|x_i-a_m|$ and
$u\mapsto u/|x_i-x_j|$ is $K$-bounded with $K$-bound zero: for every
$\eta>0$ there is a finite constant $C_\eta$ with
$$\Bigl\|\frac{u}{|x_i-a_m|}\Bigr\|_2\le\eta\|Ku\|_2+C_\eta\|u\|_2,\qquad \Bigl\|\frac{u}{|x_i-x_j|}\Bigr\|_2\le\eta\|Ku\|_2+C_\eta\|u\|_2$$
for all $u\in D(K)$ ([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]],
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]);

(b) $D(K)\subseteq D(M_V)$, and $M_V$ is symmetric on $D(K)$ with $K$-bound
zero; consequently
$$H:=K+M_V,\qquad D(H):=D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C),$$
is self-adjoint and bounded below, and $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$
is a core for $H$ ([[thm-kato-rellich]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(c) the operator $K\otimes I_r+M_V\otimes I_r$ on
$L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)\otimes\mathbb C^r$ with domain $D(K)\otimes\mathbb C^r$
is self-adjoint and bounded below;

(d) if $m_1=\cdots=m_N=m$ and the coefficients are permutation invariant
($z_{im}$ independent of $i$ and $z_{ij}$ independent of the pair), then the
transported permutation unitaries of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]]
reduce $H$, and the restrictions of $H$ to the symmetric and antisymmetric
sectors are self-adjoint on those sectors.

No Hunziker-van Winter-Zhislin threshold statement, no uniform-in-$N$
stability, no thermodynamic limit, no spectral statement beyond
self-adjointness and boundedness from below, and no physical interpretation of
$H$, the masses or the coefficients is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Work on a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first variable. Let $A$ be self-adjoint and let $B$ be symmetric with $D(A)\subseteq D(B)$ and
$A$-bound less than one ([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]).
Then $A+B$ with domain $D(A)$ is self-adjoint. If $A$ is merely essentially
self-adjoint and $B$ is symmetric with $D(A)\subseteq D(B)$ and $A$-bound less
than one, then $A+B$ on $D(A)$ is essentially self-adjoint and its closure is
the self-adjoint operator obtained by applying the first part to $\overline A$
and the graph-norm extension of $B|_{D(A)}$ to $D(\overline A)$. If $A\ge\gamma$ and
$(a,b)$ is an admissible pair for $B$ with $a<1$, then
$A+B\ge\gamma-\max\{a|\gamma|+b,\ b/(1-a)\}$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to \mathbb C$ belong to
$L^1(\mu \times \nu)$. Then:

1. for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the section $f_x$ belongs to $L^1(\nu)$;
2. for $\nu$-almost every $y$, the section $f^y$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$;
3. after assigning the value $0$ on the exceptional parameter sets, the
   section-integral functions are integrable; and
4. the three integrals agree:
$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

derivations.claim: [Unit preparations in the actual combined sector] Orthonormality of $u,v$ makes $u\otimes v$ and $v\otimes u$ orthogonal unit vectors, so $\varphi_\pm$ and $f_\pm$ are unit and satisfy $f_\pm(y,x)=\pm f_\pm(x,y)$. The displayed spin definitions give $\|\chi_\pm\|=1$ and $R\chi_\pm=\pm\chi_\pm$. Hence $\mathcal U(f_\pm\chi_\mp)(x,y)=R f_\pm(y,x)\chi_\mp=-f_\pm(x,y)\chi_\mp$. Their $L^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$ norm is one. By [F1], $\Phi_\pm=\Theta_2^{-1}(f_\pm\chi_\mp)$ are unit vectors in the declared $\mathfrak H_2^-$, so their pure projectors define the declared preparations. This proves (a).

[H² domain and exact one-body expectation] By [F5], each spatial product is in $H^2(\mathbb R^6)$, hence so is $f_\pm$. Multiplication by the fixed finite spin vector means a finite tuple of constant scalar multiples of $f_\pm$, so $f_\pm\chi_\mp\in H^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$. Step 1.1 and [F4] then place $\Phi_\pm$ in the exact domain of $H_2^-$. Write $q(x,y)=u(x)v(y)$, $r(x,y)=v(x)u(y)$ and $L=-a\Delta_x-a\Delta_y+V_b$. By [F5], $Lq=(hu)(x)v(y)+u(x)(hv)(y)$ and $Lr=(hv)(x)u(y)+v(x)(hu)(y)$. Fubini gives $\langle Lq,q\rangle=\langle Lr,r\rangle=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v$, and $\langle Lq,r\rangle=\langle hu,v\rangle\langle v,u\rangle+\langle u,v\rangle\langle hv,u\rangle=0$; the reversed cross pairing vanishes in the same way. Thus $\langle Lf_\pm,f_\pm\rangle=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v$. Spin independence and $\|\chi_\mp\|=1$ give the same pairing in the full spin representation. The unbounded slot terms all had their stated domain inputs.

[Pair expectation and reality] In the bounded case, absolute values of $D$ and $X$ are bounded by $\|W\|_\infty\|u\|_2^2\|v\|_2^2$; the crossed term uses $\int|uv|\le\|u\|_2\|v\|_2$. In the Coulomb case $H^2\subset H^1$, so [F3] gives absolute convergence and $f_\pm\in D(M_W)$. For either real even kernel, exchanging $x,y$ in the absolutely convergent $X$ integral gives $X=\overline X$; the two direct diagonal terms are equal to $D$. Expanding $|f_\pm|^2$ therefore gives $\langle M_Wf_\pm,f_\pm\rangle=D\pm X$, as in [F3]. The full spin-independent pair multiplier has exactly this expectation in $f_\pm\chi_\mp$. No orbitals were required to be real.

The unitary $\Theta_2$ preserves the energy pairings. Combining the one-body result of step 2.1 and pair result of step 3.1 gives $m_{\rho_\pm}(H_2^-)=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v+D\pm X$. This proves (d) and completes the statement.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak H$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension
$d\ge1$ with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $H:\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$ be a self-adjoint
linear operator with real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_d$ (repeated according to
multiplicity) and orthonormal eigenbasis $(v_1,\dots,v_d)$, and let $\beta>0$.
Write
$$Z:=\sum_{j=1}^d e^{-\beta E_j}\in(0,\infty),\qquad \rho_\beta:=\frac1Z\sum_{j=1}^d e^{-\beta E_j}T_{v_j,v_j},$$
where $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). Let
$\mathcal D$ be the set of density operators on $\mathfrak H$, i.e. positive
self-adjoint trace-class operators $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]), and
for $\rho\in\mathcal D$ with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_d\ge0$ (counted with
multiplicity and in any order) define the entropy
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log d]$$
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). Then:

(a) $\rho_\beta\in\mathcal D$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\frac1Z\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}E_j$,
and
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z ;$$

(b) for every $\rho\in\mathcal D$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)\ \ge\ -\beta^{-1}\log Z ;$$

(c) for every $\rho\in\mathcal D$, $s(\rho)\le\log d$, with $s(\rho)=\log d$ if
and only if $\rho=d^{-1}\,\mathrm{id}$; when $H=0$ one has $Z=d$,
$\rho_\beta=d^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ and the bound in (b) is attained there.

The combination $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ is a purely
mathematical functional of $(\rho,H,\beta)$; identifying $\beta$ with an
inverse physical temperature and $\rho_\beta$ with a thermal equilibrium state
are additional physical assumptions not asserted here.

For $x>0$, $\log$ is differentiable and
$$\log'(x)=\frac1x,\qquad \log x=\int_1^x\frac{dt}{t}.$$

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and

derivations.claim: [The canonical preparation and its data] By [F1], $Z_N=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ is a finite sum with $0<Z_N<\infty$; since $D\ge1$ each term is positive, so $q_j=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N>0$ with $\sum_jq_j=1$. By [F1] the operator $\rho_\beta=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ is a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, hence a declared sector preparation of the model, and the two displayed identities are the clauses of [F1] together with the entropy definition. This proves (a).

[Strict scalar defects, including zero weights] By [F3] and the mean value theorem applied to $\log$ between $1$ and $t>0$, $t\ne1$, one has $\log t=(t-1)/\xi$ with $\xi$ strictly between $1$ and $t$; for $t>1$ this is less than $t-1$, and for $0<t<1$ it is also less than $t-1$ because the numerator is negative and $\xi<1$. Thus $\log t\le t-1$, with equality exactly at $t=1$. For $w\ge0$, $r>0$ define $b(w,r):=w\log(w/r)$ when $w>0$ and $b(0,r):=0$, and $d(w,r):=b(w,r)-w+r$. If $w>0$, apply the bound to $t=r/w$ and the quotient law to get $d(w,r)\ge0$, with equality exactly at $w=r$; if $w=0$, $d(0,r)=r>0$. Likewise $h(q,r):=\log r+(q-r)/r-\log q\ge0$ for $q,r>0$, with equality exactly at $q=r$, by applying the bound to $t=q/r$.

[The degenerate case] If $H_N^\sigma=c\,\mathrm{id}$ then $E_j=c$ for all $j$ and [F1] gives $Z_N=De^{-\beta c}$, $q_j=D^{-1}$, $\rho_\beta=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$; by [F1] $s(\rho_\beta)=\log D$ and $F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_BT\log(De^{-\beta c})=c-k_BT\log D$. This proves (d).

[The free-energy difference for every mixed preparation] Let $\rho=\sum_iw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ be as in [F2] and put $p_{ij}=|\langle u_i,v_j\rangle|^2$, $r_i=\sum_jp_{ij}q_j$. Each $r_i>0$ and $\sum_ir_i=\sum_jq_j\sum_ip_{ij}=1$. Use the entropy convention $\eta(w)=w\log w$ for $w>0$ and $\eta(0)=0$ (the notation $0\log0=0$ does not define $\log0$). The trace pairing and the entropy definition give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)=\sum_{i,j}w_ip_{ij}E_j$ and $s(\rho)=-\sum_i\eta(w_i)$. Since $\beta E_j=-\log q_j-\log Z_N$, $\Delta:=\beta(F(\rho)-F_{\mathrm{eq}})=\sum_i\bigl(\eta(w_i)-w_i\sum_jp_{ij}\log q_j\bigr)$. Define $a_i:=\log r_i-\sum_jp_{ij}\log q_j=\sum_jp_{ij}h(q_j,r_i)$, the last equality using $\sum_jp_{ij}=1$ and $\sum_jp_{ij}(q_j-r_i)=0$. Step 1.2 gives $a_i\ge0$, with equality exactly when $q_j=r_i$ for every $j$ with $p_{ij}>0$. By the quotient law for positive $w_i$ and by the explicit zero convention otherwise, $\Delta=\sum_i b(w_i,r_i)+\sum_iw_i a_i=\sum_i d(w_i,r_i)+\sum_iw_i a_i$, because $\sum_i(w_i-r_i)=0$. All summands are nonnegative, so $F(\rho)\ge F_{\mathrm{eq}}$, proving (b) for every density operator, including those with zero eigenvalues.

[Equality, strict zero-weight exclusion and degeneracies] If $F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$, the finite sum of nonnegative defects in step 2.1 vanishes. Hence $d(w_i,r_i)=0$ for every $i$; step 1.2 gives $w_i=r_i>0$, since $d(0,r_i)=r_i>0$ excludes every zero weight. Thus $w_i a_i=0$ forces $a_i=0$ for every row, and step 2.1 gives $q_j=r_i=w_i$ whenever $p_{ij}>0$. In the expansion of $u_i$ in the orthonormal basis $(v_j)$, the coefficients at all $q_j\ne w_i$ therefore vanish, so $\rho_\beta u_i=w_i u_i$. Since also $\rho u_i=w_i u_i$ and $(u_i)$ is a basis, the two operators agree: $\rho=\rho_\beta$. This argument allows arbitrary changes of basis within any repeated-eigenvalue Gibbs eigenspace. Conversely $\rho=\rho_\beta$ gives equality by [F1]. Together with step 2.1, this proves (c) with no full-rank assumption on the competing preparation.

[Conclusion and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), step 2.1 proves (b), step 3.1 proves (c), and step 1.3 proves (d). The argument is an optimisation inside the declared finite-dimensional sector at the adopted ensemble parameters; no equilibration, rate, thermodynamic limit or measured thermal quantity entered, which is (e).
