Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\omega>0$ and
$\beta>0$ be real parameters, let $F(\mathbb C)$ be the one-mode Fock space
with its complete orthonormal family $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ and number
operator $N$ as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]], and define the
operator $G_\beta\in\mathcal B(F(\mathbb C))$ by
$$G_\beta e_n:=e^{-\beta\omega n}e_n\qquad(n\in\mathbb N)$$
together with bounded linear extension. Then:

(a) $G_\beta$ is a bounded self-adjoint positive operator with $\|G_\beta\|=1$,
and $G_\beta=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb N}e^{-\beta\omega n}\,\mathrm{id}$ on the
Fock sectors ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]);

(b) the series of weights converge,
$$Z(\beta):=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}e^{-\beta\omega n}=\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\omega}},\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,e^{-\beta\omega n}=\frac{e^{-\beta\omega}}{(1-e^{-\beta\omega})^2};$$

(c) $G_\beta$ is trace class with
$\|G_\beta\|_1=\operatorname{tr}G_\beta=Z(\beta)$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);

(d) $\rho_\beta:=G_\beta/Z(\beta)$ is a density operator on $F(\mathbb C)$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]), and its
number expectation, defined by the absolutely convergent spectral sum
$\langle N\rangle_\beta:=\sum_{n}n\,e^{-\beta\omega n}/Z(\beta)$, equals
$$\langle N\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\omega}}{1-e^{-\beta\omega}}=\frac1{e^{\beta\omega}-1};$$
more generally $\sum_nn^k e^{-\beta\omega n}<\infty$ for every $k\ge1$.

The parameter $\beta$ is a positive real parameter of the model; its
identification with an inverse temperature, and the interpretation of
$\rho_\beta$ as a physical thermal state, are additional physical assumptions
not asserted here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\beta>0$ and let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$ and
$\mu\in\mathbb R$ be real data; write $q_j:=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)}$.

(a) *Single fermionic orbital.* On $\mathfrak h:=\mathbb C^2$ with orthonormal
basis $(u_0,u_1)$ define the bounded self-adjoint operator $N_-$ by
$N_-u_0=0$, $N_-u_1=u_1$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Then the diagonal
operator $F:=\sum_{k=0}^1e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}\,T_{u_k,u_k}$ is
positive, self-adjoint, finite rank, and
$$\operatorname{tr}F=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)},\qquad \frac{\sum_{k=0}^1k\,e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}}{\operatorname{tr}F}=\frac1{e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1}$$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]],
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(b) *Countable grand-canonical factor products.* Define
$\mathcal N:=\{N\subseteq\{1,2,\dots\}:N\text{ finite}\}$ and set
$$Z_{\mathrm B}:=\sup_{N\in\mathcal N}\ \prod_{j\in N}\frac1{1-q_j}\in(0,\infty],\qquad Z_{\mathrm F}:=\sup_{N\in\mathcal N}\ \prod_{j\in N}(1+q_j)\in[1,\infty],$$
with the convention $Z_{\mathrm B}:=+\infty$ if some $j$ has
$\varepsilon_j-\mu\le0$. Then:
$$Z_{\mathrm B}<\infty\iff\sum_j e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty \ \text{ and }\ \mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j,\qquad Z_{\mathrm F}<\infty\iff\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty,$$
and in these finite cases $Z_{\mathrm B}=\prod_{j\ge1}(1-q_j)^{-1}$ and
$Z_{\mathrm F}=\prod_{j\ge1}(1+q_j)$.

(c) *Mode occupancies and dilute remainders.* For a single mode with
$0<q<1$ (boson) and $q>0$ (fermion),
$$\frac{\sum_{n\ge0}n\,q^n}{\sum_{n\ge0}q^n}=\frac q{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q},\qquad \frac{\sum_{n=0}^1n\,q^n}{\sum_{n=0}^1q^n}=\frac q{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q};$$
consequently the deviations from $q$ are bounded by $q^2/(1-q)$ and
$q^2/(1+q)$ respectively, and both are at most $2q^2$ when $q\le1/2$.

All statements are mathematical statements about diagonal weights and products;
no identification of $\beta,\mu,\varepsilon_j$ with physical temperatures,
chemical potentials or energies, and no thermal or thermodynamic conclusion,
is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with a countable complete orthonormal family $(e_j)_{j\ge1}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$, let $\beta>0$, and let
$F(H)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]. Let
$\mathcal M$ be the set of finite nondecreasing sequences
$I=(j_1\le\cdots\le j_n)$ with $n\ge0$ (the empty sequence included); for
$I=(j_1\le\cdots\le j_n)$ put
$$v_I:=P_+^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})\in F(H)\quad(n\ge1),\qquad v_{\varnothing}:=\Omega,\qquad \lambda_I:=\varepsilon_{j_1}+\cdots+\varepsilon_{j_n}\ (\text{empty sum }0),$$
and $u_I:=v_I/\|v_I\|$. Then:

(a) $(u_I)_{I\in\mathcal M}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(H)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]);

(b) the diagonal operator
$$D(D_\beta):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-2\beta\lambda_I}|\langle\psi,u_I\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad D_\beta\psi:=\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}\langle\psi,u_I\rangle u_I$$
is bounded, self-adjoint and positive with $\|D_\beta\|\le1$; it is trace class
exactly when $\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}<\infty$, and then
$\operatorname{tr}D_\beta=\sum_Ie^{-\beta\lambda_I}$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);

(c) for every $N\ge1$, $\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{I\in\mathcal M\\ I\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}}}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\prod_{j=1}^N\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}$, and
$$\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\lim_{N\to\infty}\prod_{j=1}^N\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}\in(0,\infty];$$

(d) *product criterion*: $\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}<\infty$ if and only if
$\sum_{j\ge1}e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$, and in that case
$$\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\prod_{j=1}^\infty\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}<\infty ;$$

(e) consequently $D_\beta$ is trace class if and only if
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$, with the trace given by the infinite
product in (d).

The operator $D_\beta$ is a purely mathematical diagonal operator on $F(H)$;
no thermal, thermodynamic or measurement interpretation is asserted.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric
projections $P_+^{(n)}$ and Fock space $F(H)$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]. Define the
number operator by
$$D(N):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (N\psi)_n:=n\psi_n .$$
Then:

(a) $N$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $F(H)$ with the displayed
domain; $N\ge0$ in the sense that $\langle N\psi,\psi\rangle\ge0$ for
$\psi\in D(N)$, $N\Omega=0$, and $F_0$ is a core for $N$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(b) for every $n$, every nonzero $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ satisfies
$N\iota_n(u)=n\,\iota_n(u)$, and for $H\ne\{0\}$ the spectrum of $N$ is
$\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$;

(c) for $f\in H$ and $\psi\in F_0$ the core operators of
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]] satisfy
$$N S_+(f)\psi-S_+(f)N\psi=S_+(f)\psi,\qquad N S_-(f)\psi-S_-(f)N\psi=-S_-(f)\psi ;$$

(d) $D(N)\subseteq D_1:=\{\psi:\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, and for every
$\psi\in D(N)$,
$$\|N\psi\|^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2,\qquad \langle N\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\|\psi_n\|^2 .$$

No physical interpretation of $N$, and no assertion about particle number
measurement, is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with a supplied countably infinite orthonormal basis $(e_j)_{j\ge1}$, let $N\ge1$ be an integer, and let $\varepsilon_j\in\mathbb R$ with $\varepsilon_j\ge b$ for a fixed $b\in\mathbb R$. Use the completed tensor power and permutation-sector projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]], and write $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$ for $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$. Then:

(a) For every finitely supported sequence $n=(n_j)_{j\ge1}$ of nonnegative integers with $\sum_jn_j=N$, put $\operatorname{orb}(n):=\{(i_1,\ldots,i_N):\#\{k:i_k=j\}=n_j\text{ for every }j\}$ and
$$b_n^+:=|\operatorname{orb}(n)|^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in\operatorname{orb}(n)}e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}.$$
For every $N$-element subset $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ of the positive integers, put
$$b_J^-:=\frac1{\sqrt{N!}}\sum_{\pi\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)e_{j_{\widehat{\pi}(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\widehat{\pi}(N)}}.$$
These are orthonormal bases of the symmetric and antisymmetric sectors respectively. Denote their countable index sets by $\mathcal C_N^+$ and $\mathcal C_N^-$, and write $b_c^\sigma$ for the corresponding vector. Define $E_n:=\sum_jn_j\varepsilon_j$ and $E_J:=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$.

(b) The fixed-$N$ free energy operator is the self-adjoint diagonal operator
$$D(H_N^\sigma):=\left\{\psi=\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}a_cb_c^\sigma:\sum_c|E_c|^2|a_c|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad H_N^\sigma\psi:=\sum_cE_ca_cb_c^\sigma.$$
It is bounded below by $Nb$, and is the closure of its action on finite occupation sums. On elementary tensors of modes it agrees with the restriction of the labelled energy sum $\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{i_k}$, with the same diagonal-domain closure. Its spectral PVM is
$$E_N^\sigma(B)\psi=\sum_c\mathbf1_B(E_c)a_cb_c^\sigma.$$

(c) For $\beta>0$, let $q_j:=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}>0$, so $q_j\le e^{-\beta b}$. Define the extended positive trace of a bounded positive operator as its nonnegative diagonal sum in the supplied occupation basis; its independence of any other supplied orthonormal basis is proved below. With this trace (allowed to be $+\infty$),
$$Z_N^+(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H_N^+}=h_N(q):=\sum_{1\le i_1\le\cdots\le i_N}q_{i_1}\cdots q_{i_N},$$
$$Z_N^-(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H_N^-}=e_N(q):=\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_N}q_{i_1}\cdots q_{i_N}.$$
All sums are nonnegative-series sums. For either sign,
$$\left(\prod_{k=1}^{N-1}q_k\right)\sum_{j=N}^\infty q_j\le Z_N^\sigma(\beta)\le\left(\sum_{j=1}^\infty q_j\right)^N.$$
For $N=1$ the product is $1$, the tail starts at $1$, and both partition sums equal $\sum_jq_j$. Consequently, for every fixed $N\ge1$ and either statistics,
$$0<Z_N^\sigma(\beta)<\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_j e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty.$$
The bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$ is trace class exactly in this case, and its ordinary trace then equals the displayed occupation sum. This is a fixed-$N$ criterion, not a trace over all particle numbers.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert
space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Let
$H^{\otimes 0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes 1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(n+1)}:=H^{\otimes n}\widehat\otimes H$ be the completed tensor
powers with elementary tensors $u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); for $n\ge 1$ let
$P_+^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ be the symmetric projection of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] and set
$P_+^{(0)}:=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}$. Write $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ for
its range and define

$$F(H):=\Bigl\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}:\ \psi_n\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\ \text{for all }n,\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$

Then:

(a) for $\psi,\varphi\in F(H)$ the scalar series
$\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle$ converges absolutely and
defines a sesquilinear form, linear in the first argument, with respect to
which $F(H)$ is a complex vector space with inner product
$\langle\psi,\varphi\rangle:=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle$
([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]],
[[def-series-and-absolute-convergence-in-a-normed-space]]);

(b) $(F(H),\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ is a Hilbert space, i.e. the induced norm
is complete ([[def-hilbert-space]]);

(c) the vacuum vector $\Omega:=(1,0,0,\dots)$ satisfies $\|\Omega\|=1$, and the
finite-particle space
$F_0:=\{\psi\in F(H):\psi_n=0\ \text{for all but finitely many }n\}$ is a dense
linear subspace of $F(H)$ ([[def-dense-top]]);

(d) for every $n$ the map
$\iota_n:\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\to F(H)$,
$\iota_n(u):=(0,\dots,0,u,0,\dots)$ (entry in coordinate $n$) is a linear
isometry of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ onto the closed subspace of vectors
supported in coordinate $n$;

(e) if $H$ admits a countable complete orthonormal family
$(e_i)_{i\in I}$, $I$ at most countable
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
then $F(H)$ is separable ([[def-separable-space]]);

(f) *direct sums of self-adjoint operators*: if for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
including $n=0$, a self-adjoint operator $T_n$ on the Hilbert space
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with domain
$D(T_n)\subseteq\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ is given (so $T_0$ is a
self-adjoint operator on $\mathbb C$),
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-unbounded-linear-operator-domain-and-graph]]), and

$$D(T):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \psi_n\in D(T_n)\ \text{for all }n,\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (T\psi)_n:=T_n\psi_n,$$

then $T$ is self-adjoint and $D(T)$ is dense; if in addition every $T_n$ is
bounded with $\sup_{n}\|T_n\|<\infty$, then $T$ is bounded with
$\|T\|=\sup_n\|T_n\|$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

No physical interpretation of $F(H)$, of the tensor powers or of the direct-sum
operators is asserted.

derivations.claim: [The single bosonic mode] Apply [F1] with $\omega=\varepsilon$: $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical preparation of the declared energy operator $\varepsilon N$, the number readout $N$ is self-adjoint with $Ne_n=ne_n$ by [F4], and its thermal mean in $\rho_\beta$ equals the absolutely convergent sum $\sum_nnq^n/\sum_nq^n=1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1)$ with $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$; all higher moments are finite by [F1]. This proves (a).

[The fermionic orbital and the shift] For the stated arbitrary real $\varepsilon_1,\mu$, direct evaluation in the two occupation vectors gives the unnormalized positive operator $G=\sum_{k=0}^1q^kT_{u_k,u_k}$ with $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}>0$ and $\operatorname{tr}G=Z=1+q$. Thus $F=G/Z$ has trace one and occupation mean $q/(1+q)=1/(e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1)$ with $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}$; for $\mu=0$, $\varepsilon_1>0$ this is the model's thermal mean at the declared energy $\varepsilon_1$. This proves (b) and the identities of (d).

[The product criterion] Declare the occupation-space effective generator $G$ by $G b_n=\sum_j(\varepsilon_j-\mu)n_j b_n$, including the vacuum with eigenvalue zero; its domain is the set of coefficient families whose squared-energy weighted sum is finite. The occupation bases and [F5] make this a supplied self-adjoint realization of $H-\mu\mathcal N$ as required by the ensemble postulate. In the finite bosonic-partition case all shifted energies are positive, so $G\ge0$. In the finite fermionic-partition case summability implies $\varepsilon_j\to\infty$, hence only finitely many shifted energies are negative, and every fermionic configuration contains each at most once; their finite sum is a lower bound for $G$. Coordinate spectral projections and bounded exponential integration then identify $e^{-\beta G}$ with the diagonal occupation weights. Applying the criterion [F3] to the free-mode energies with chemical-potential shift and combining with the finite products of [F2] gives the stated equivalences for the bosonic and fermionic products, under the stated conditions $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j$ (bosons) and no further condition (fermions). This proves (c); normalized weights are the additionally adopted Gibbs preparation, not a derivation of physical equilibration.

[Readings] In each case the occupation number is an assigned sharp observable by [F4], so the mean of its outcome law in the canonical preparation is the number computed in steps 1.1-1.3; the identification of the computed parameters with a physical temperature and chemical potential is the adopted assumption of the ensemble postulate, and no convergence statement beyond the displayed criteria is asserted. This gives the readings of (a)-(d).

[Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1-1.3 and 2.1 prove (a)-(d). The argument is a finite-mode or product computation at assigned temperature; no thermodynamic limit, continuum of modes, condensation or measured occupation entered, which is (e).

citations.quote:
**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P4 together with P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P4, P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics, assert no dynamics for a prescribed time-dependent family or for an open system (clauses (iv) and (v) of P4 are separate model assumptions treated on their own pages), assert no measurement model, no apparatus realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any laboratory system is exactly isolated.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

**(a) Adopted readings and restricted sector class.** Adopt the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], for the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]. This definition
applies to the class of declared models whose sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is **finite-dimensional**, in particular to every
finite-mode realization
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]), where
$D:=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is finite (and may be zero) by
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a),
(b). Write $\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$ for the set of declared sector
preparations, that is, the density operators on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
If $D=0$, the only operator has trace zero, so
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)=\varnothing$. The partition trace is
$Z_N=0$, and there is no normalized canonical density or equilibrium free
energy; $\log D$, $D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ and $\log Z_N$ are not used in this
branch. Clauses (b), (d) and (e) below apply when $D\ge1$; the assigned
parameters of (c) can still be declared when $D=0$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) Dimensionless entropy.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$
with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_D\ge0$ (counted with multiplicity, in any
order), the **entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log D],$$
the quantity of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]]
clause (a) with $\log$ the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). It is dimensionless, is a function of the
eigenvalue multiset of $\rho$ alone, and equals zero exactly for pure
preparations; by clause (c) of the cited theorem $s(\rho)=\log D$ holds
exactly when $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$.

**(c) Boltzmann constant, temperature and inverse temperature.** The model
assigns a positive **Boltzmann constant** $k_B$ and a positive **temperature**
$T$; in the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the unit of $k_B$ is
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$, the unit of $T$ is the kelvin, and
$$k_B=1.380\,649\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$$
fixed exactly by the BIPM SI definition. The model declares the **inverse
temperature** $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$, a positive real number in $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
The value and exactness of $k_B$ are unit-convention facts; the assignment of
the parameter $T$ to a physical sample, and the identification of
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature, are adopted
assumptions of the ensemble model of this pair, not consequences of P1-P4,
and are tested identifications with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus postulate P7.

**(d) Physical entropy.** The **physical entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$S(\rho):=k_B\,s(\rho),$$
read in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$. It is nonnegative, is at most
$k_B\log D$, and vanishes exactly for pure preparations.

**(e) Free-energy functional.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$,
let $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)\in\mathbb R$ be the mean of the
declared energy observable in $\rho$ (finite because $D<\infty$, in the
moment reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).
The **Helmholtz free-energy reading** of $\rho$ is
$$F(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho),$$
read in joules; it is the quantity
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a)
at the identified $\beta$. For the canonical operator
$\rho_\beta:=e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}/Z_N$ and
$Z_N:=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}\in(0,\infty)$ (positive finite sum in the
nonzero finite-dimensional sector), the number $F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$
is called the **equilibrium free energy**; it is the value of the functional
at $\rho_\beta$ by the cited theorem.

**(f) Scope.** This definition covers only declared models with
finite-dimensional sector space, with the zero-sector branch of (a), and preparations in
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$. For a declared spatial realization, whose
sector space is infinite-dimensional, the operator $\rho\log\rho$ need not be
trace class; no entropy, physical entropy or free energy is defined here for
that case, and a separate trace-class statement would be required. The
definition asserts no increase of entropy in time, no equilibration to
$\rho_\beta$, no thermodynamic limit, no pressure or volume variable, and no
measured temperature, entropy or free energy.

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak H$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension
$d\ge1$ with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $H:\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$ be a self-adjoint
linear operator with real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_d$ (repeated according to
multiplicity) and orthonormal eigenbasis $(v_1,\dots,v_d)$, and let $\beta>0$.
Write
$$Z:=\sum_{j=1}^d e^{-\beta E_j}\in(0,\infty),\qquad \rho_\beta:=\frac1Z\sum_{j=1}^d e^{-\beta E_j}T_{v_j,v_j},$$
where $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). Let
$\mathcal D$ be the set of density operators on $\mathfrak H$, i.e. positive
self-adjoint trace-class operators $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]), and
for $\rho\in\mathcal D$ with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_d\ge0$ (counted with
multiplicity and in any order) define the entropy
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log d]$$
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). Then:

(a) $\rho_\beta\in\mathcal D$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\frac1Z\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}E_j$,
and
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z ;$$

(b) for every $\rho\in\mathcal D$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)\ \ge\ -\beta^{-1}\log Z ;$$

(c) for every $\rho\in\mathcal D$, $s(\rho)\le\log d$, with $s(\rho)=\log d$ if
and only if $\rho=d^{-1}\,\mathrm{id}$; when $H=0$ one has $Z=d$,
$\rho_\beta=d^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ and the bound in (b) is attained there.

The combination $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ is a purely
mathematical functional of $(\rho,H,\beta)$; identifying $\beta$ with an
inverse physical temperature and $\rho_\beta$ with a thermal equilibrium state
are additional physical assumptions not asserted here.

**(a) Adopted readings and framework data.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable
and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4) and the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7), together with the
Boltzmann-constant and temperature conventions of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Declare one of the
following model readings of the same **adopted Gibbs assignment**:

(i) a fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]], on its sector space,
with Gibbs generator $G:=H_N^\sigma$; or

(ii) a separately declared number-variable mode model, such as a one-mode
bosonic Fock space, a fermionic occupation space, or a declared countable
independent-mode space, with its declared assigned observables and energy
operator $H$. The model declares a self-adjoint Gibbs generator $G$ on that
space: either $G=H$, or a separately supplied self-adjoint realization of the
effective generator $G=H-\mu\mathcal N$, where $\mathcal N$ is the declared
particle-number operator and $\mu\in\mathbb R$ is an assigned chemical
potential in joules. The subtraction is an operator with its supplied domain,
not an assertion that a formal unbounded difference is self-adjoint.

In either reading assume $G$ is bounded below and give its spectral PVM
$E_G$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Let $T>0$ be an assigned temperature in
kelvin and let $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$ with the assigned
Boltzmann constant $k_B$. The Gibbs assignment to either model, and the
chemical-potential identification in (ii), are additional physical
preparation assumptions made here; they are not derived from P1-P4 or from
the fixed-$N$ construction. In (ii) no restriction on the assigned real
$\mu$ is imposed beyond the declared generator and trace existence
conditions; the mode-specific convergence conditions are proved separately.
For reading (ii), $G$ specifies the Gibbs weights. If the assigned autonomous
dynamics is generated by $H$, stationarity of the Gibbs density requires its
separate dynamical or commutation hypotheses; this assignment does not
identify $H-\mu\mathcal N$ with the physical evolution generator.
The physical Helmholtz free-energy vocabulary of the entropy definition
continues to apply only to its stated nonzero finite-sector class and is not
extended to every effective generator by this postulate.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral calculus.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** The model assumes
that the **partition trace is strictly positive and finite**:
$$0<Z:=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta G}<\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}B:=\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\langle Bf,f\rangle$ for a
bounded positive $B$ and an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$, with value allowed
to be $+\infty$. Such a basis exists under the declared AC by the maximal
orthonormal-family argument using [[thm-zorn]] and the zero-complement
criterion of [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]].
This trace is basis independent: for $C:=B^{1/2}$ of
[[thm-positive-square-root]], the defining sum is
$\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\|Cf\|^2$, whose invariance is
[[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]]. When the sum is finite,
$C$ is Hilbert-Schmidt ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), so $B=C^2$ is
trace class by [[thm-trace-class-iff-product-of-two-hilbert-schmidt-operators]],
and its ordinary trace is this same diagonal sum by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Apply this to the bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta G}$, since the
declared Gibbs generator $G$ is bounded below. The model
adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared model
at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta G}.$$
If the sector is zero-dimensional, its partition trace is $Z=0$, no
trace-one density exists, and no canonical density or equilibrium free
energy is assigned. On a nonzero finite-dimensional model space, $Z$ is a
positive finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues of $G$; no energy
sign restriction is needed. There $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]], and the
strict positivity and finiteness hypothesis is automatic. In reading (i),
$Z=Z_N$ and this is precisely the finite-sector Gibbs assignment.

Outside the finite-dimensional class the existence hypothesis is a genuine
restriction. For a declared non-interacting fixed-$N$ model with a supplied
countably infinite orthonormal eigenmode basis and real mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ bounded below, the complete construction and trace criterion
of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-fixed-n-countable-mode-partition-criterion]] give
$Z_N=h_N(q)$ for bosonic statistics or $Z_N=e_N(q)$ for fermionic statistics,
where $q_j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}$ and $h_N,e_N$ are the corresponding
nonnegative occupation-series sums. For every fixed $N\ge1$, either trace is
finite exactly when $\sum_jq_j<\infty$. This is a trace on the fixed-$N$
sector and permits negative mode energies.

For the separately declared full bosonic Fock models of reading (ii),
the single-mode calculation of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] and the product
criterion of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]
provide the separate mathematical full-Fock traces, with their original
positive mode-energy hypotheses: they sum over every particle number,
including the vacuum, giving $(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$ for one mode
and $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j})^{-1}$ for countably many modes.
Their physical Gibbs reading is the additional assignment of (a)(ii), not a
consequence of a mathematical trace formula. Those full-Fock traces are not
substituted for the fixed-$N$ partition trace of reading (i).

**(c) The equilibrium assumption and thermal means.** The model **assumes**
that, for a declared sample of the species at the assigned temperature $T$
and in the absence of further preparation information, the preparation
description of the sample is $\rho_\beta$ in the sense of P1. For an assigned
sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ with spectral PVM $E_A$, define its outcome law
$\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta E_A(B))$ as in
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).
If and only if the absolute first moment is finite,
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a)<\infty,$$
the model defines the **thermal mean** at temperature $T$ by
$$\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R}a\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a),$$
read in the assigned unit $u_A$. For bounded $A$ this equals
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$. For
unbounded $A$, if the mean exists and the literal product $A\rho_\beta$ is
defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class, the mean also equals
$\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$ and
$\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho_\beta A})$; these conditional product
identities are proved by the density eigenexpansion in
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-spectral-mean-and-defined-trace-product]]. First-moment
existence alone imposes no such product or operator-square-domain condition.
When the absolute first moment is infinite the model asserts no finite
thermal mean. The identification of the parameter $T$ with the thermodynamic temperature of a
sample, and of $\beta$ with its inverse temperature, is part of this
assumption; the stated conservation and equilibrium properties of
$\rho_\beta$ under the flow of P4, and the extremal property of $\rho_\beta$
among preparations, are separate conditional results of this pair.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the corresponding functional built from $G$.
Its physical Helmholtz free-energy reading applies in the stated finite
fixed-sector class; an effective-generator interpretation in a different
mode model is a separate declared reading. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

**(e) Scope.** The postulate asserts nothing about how a sample reaches the
Gibbs preparation; in particular it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration
time, no ergodicity, no master-equation or Markov approximation, no
thermodynamic limit, no pressure, volume or phase-transition structure, and
no measured temperature or expectation. The requirement $0<Z<\infty$ is part
of the assumption; the model does not define a canonical preparation when
$Z=0$ or the partition trace diverges. Any comparison with a laboratory sample requires the
declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7, and
agreement of a thermal prediction with data is evidence about the combined
model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework or of this
postulate.

derivations.claim: [Entropy conservation] Let $\rho(0)=\sum_iw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ be the spectral decomposition of [F2]. By [F1], $U(t)$ is unitary, so $(U(t)u_i)$ is an orthonormal basis and $\rho(t)=\sum_iw_iT_{U(t)u_i,U(t)u_i}$: the eigenvalues of $\rho(t)$ are the same $w_i$ with the same multiplicities. By [F2] the entropy depends only on that multiset, so $s(\rho(t))=s(\rho(0))$ for every $t$. This proves (a).

[Stationarity of the canonical preparation] By [F3] $\rho_\beta$ is diagonal in the eigenbasis $(v_j)$ of $H_N^\sigma$; the same basis diagonalizes $U(t)$ with eigenvalues $e^{-itE_j/\hbar}$, so $U(t)T_{v_j,v_j}U(t)^*=T_{v_j,v_j}$ for every $j$ and hence $U(t)\rho_\beta U(t)^*=\rho_\beta$. Every thermal mean $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)$ is therefore time independent by [F1]. This proves (b).

[No unitary production of the canonical preparation] Suppose $\rho(t)=\rho_\beta$ for some $t$. Applying the unitary $U(t)^*$ on both sides and using $U(t)^*=U(t)^{-1}$ from [F1], $\rho(0)=U(t)^*\rho_\beta U(t)=\rho_\beta$ by step 1.2 applied to $-t$. Hence $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$ implies $\rho(t)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every $t$, which is (c).

[Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1-2.1 prove (a)-(c). The argument used only the unitary flow, the eigenvalue multiset of a preparation and the spectral form of $\rho_\beta$; no environment, measurement model, readout equilibration or laboratory sample entered, which is (d).
