citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\varepsilon>0$ and $\beta>0$ be real parameters, let $\mathfrak h$ be a
two-dimensional complex Hilbert space with orthonormal basis
$(u_0,u_1)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and let $H:=T_{u_1,u_1}\varepsilon=\varepsilon\,T_{u_1,u_1}$ be the
self-adjoint operator with eigenvalues $0$ on $\mathbb Cu_0$ and
$\varepsilon$ on $\mathbb Cu_1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). Let
$$Z:=\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j},\qquad \rho_\beta:=\frac1Z\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j}T_{u_j,u_j},\qquad s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i$$
be the partition sum, canonical operator and entropy of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause
(a), with $E_0=0$, $E_1=\varepsilon$ and $w_i$ the eigenvalues of a density
operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak h$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]]). Then:

(a) $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(1,2)$, and
$$\rho_\beta=\frac1Z\bigl(T_{u_0,u_0}+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}T_{u_1,u_1}\bigr)$$
is a density operator on $\mathfrak h$ that is not the maximally mixed state
$\tfrac12\mathrm{id}$;

(b) the mean energy is the exact identity
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\frac{\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{Z}=\frac{\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1},\qquad 0<\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2};$$

(c) the entropy and free energy satisfy
$$s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z+\frac{\beta\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}=\log\bigl(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\bigr)+\frac{\beta\varepsilon\,e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}},\qquad 0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log 2,$$
and, with $F:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=F ;$$

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) are exact algebraic identities for the
declared two-dimensional Hilbert space and the two real parameters
$\varepsilon,\beta>0$; no temperature, thermodynamic, equilibrium or
measurement interpretation is asserted, and the parameter $\beta$ carries no
physical dimension in this lemma.

**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

**(a) Adopted readings, units and choice hypotheses.** Adopt the state and
composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the
observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4), the non-relativistic kinematics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] (P5)
and the identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), in the state
reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable
reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
evolution reading of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
the sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]].
Let a **declared species sector** with one-particle space $H$, mass $m>0$
(kg), spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and statistics choice
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$ be given as in that definition, in the massive spin-$s$
one-particle reading of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; fix an integer
$N\ge1$ and let $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}\subseteq
H^{\otimes N}$ be the declared $N$-particle sector. All quantities below are
read in the SI conventions and units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (energies in joules). Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); the Axiom of Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) is assumed only in the Coulomb realization of
clause (d)(ii), where it is the choice hypothesis of the cited self-adjointness
theorem.

**(b) Declared one-particle data.** The model declares a one-particle
**energy operator** in one of the two following realizations.

(i) *Spatial realization.* The one-particle space is
$H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and, with $\hbar>0$ the reduced Planck
constant, the model declares a **kinetic operator** $K_1:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta$
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and a real, measurable, bounded
**external potential** $V_{\mathrm{ext}}:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ of essential
supremum $\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}\|_\infty<\infty$; the declared one-particle
operator is $h:=K_1+V_{\mathrm{ext}}(Q)$, self-adjoint by [[lem-nrqm-many-body-cc-bounded-spatial-realization]] with $N=1$, $M=2s+1$ and $a_1=\hbar^2/(2m)$, with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$. The particular singular external potential $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b-g/|x|$ is included in the Coulomb branch of clause (c)(ii), whose one-particle $h$ is specified there using the $N=1$ instance of clause (d)(ii). Any other more singular declared $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ requires a separately supplied self-adjoint realization before its operator is read as an observable.

(ii) *Finite-mode realization.* A finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space
$K$ of dimension $d\ge1$ with a declared orthonormal basis
$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) is declared together with a
self-adjoint **one-particle operator** $h\in\mathcal B(K)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).
Here the one-particle space of the species is $K$, and the assignment of the
modes $f_j$ to a laboratory mode family is a tested identification under the
preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not part of the definition.

**(c) Declared interaction.** The model declares a **pair interaction** in the
matching realization.

(i) *Bounded interaction.* In the spatial realization let
$W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be real, measurable, bounded with
$W(-z)=W(z)$ for almost every $z$ and $\|W\|_\infty<\infty$. In the
finite-mode realization let $W\in\mathcal B(K\widehat\otimes K)$ be
self-adjoint with $U_{(0\,1)}WU_{(0\,1)}=W$, where $U_{(0\,1)}$ is the exchange
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (a)
in the tensor square $\widehat{K\otimes K}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. The interaction strength
constants entering $W$ are empirical model parameters with their uncertainties
in the sense of P6 clause (iii).

(ii) *Coulomb interaction.* In the spatial realization the model may declare $W(z):=\kappa/|z|$ with a real coupling $\kappa\in\mathbb R$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m$ (repulsive for $\kappa>0$). Retain a real bounded measurable external term $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b$ as in clause (b)(i), and permit the additional singular term $-g/|x|$, where $g\in\mathbb R$ is also in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m$, so each distance denominator in metres gives an energy in joules; the total external potential is $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b(x)-g/|x|$. In this branch the declared one-particle operator is $h=K_1+M_{V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b-g/|x|}$ on $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, including the singular external term. Its self-adjointness and lower bound are the $N=1$ finite-component instance of clause (d)(ii), with no pair term. Thus the bounded one-particle reading in clause (b)(i) is replaced by this supplied Coulomb reading, rather than leaving the singular external term solely in $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$. The pair interaction still consists only of $\kappa/|x_i-x_j|$. The declared scalar potential on $\mathbb R^{3N}$ is
$$V(X)=V_b(X)+V_C(X),\qquad V_b(X)=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{\mathrm{ext}}^b(x_i),\qquad V_C(X)=-g\sum_{i=1}^N\frac1{|x_i|}+\kappa\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\frac1{|x_i-x_j|}.$$
The cases $g=0$, $\kappa=0$, $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b=0$ and either sign of either coupling are allowed. Singular values on their null collision sets are irrelevant to the multiplier classes. The singular part is supplied by [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]]; the bounded external addition is included by the exact-domain argument in clause (d)(ii), rather than attributed to a source statement which contains only the singular sum.

**(d) The labelled energy operator and its sector restriction.** Fix the
particle masses $m_1=\cdots=m_N=m$ of the declared species.

(i) *Spatial, bounded case.* Put $r_s:=2s+1$, $\mathcal S_N:=(\mathbb C^{r_s})^{\otimes N}$ and $M:=r_s^N$. The finite product spin basis identifies $\mathcal S_N$ with $\mathbb C^M$. Use the full finite-component product unitary
$$\Theta_N:H^{\otimes N}\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),\qquad [\Theta_N(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_N)]_a(X)=\prod_{j=1}^N[f_j(x_j)]_{a_j},$$
where $a\in\{1,\dots,r_s\}^N$. Its construction and combined spatial/spin permutation action are proved in [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]], from the finite-component extension of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]. For $V(X)=\sum_iV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$ define $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=-\hbar^2\Delta_X/(2m)+M_V$ componentwise. The CC-only [[lem-nrqm-many-body-cc-bounded-spatial-realization]], with $a_i=\hbar^2/(2m)$ and component count $M$, supplies self-adjointness on
$$D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)\otimes \mathcal S_N,$$
and the lower bound $-\|V\|_\infty$. Equal masses, identical external potentials and the even pair potential make the scalar domain and operator invariant under spatial block permutations. The finite-component lemma shows that the combined permutations $\mathcal U_\pi=\Theta_NU_\pi\Theta_N^{-1}$ also permute the spin slots and commute with $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ on its domain. Thus $\mathcal P_\sigma:=\Theta_NP_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta_N^{-1}$ reduces the operator by [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] (a)-(d), and the transported sector energy is
$$H_N^{\sigma,\mathrm{coord}}:=H_{\mathrm{lab}}\big|_{D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma}.$$
It is self-adjoint on $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma=\Theta_N\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, with the zero operator on the zero-sector branch. The model's tensor reading is $H_N^\sigma:=\Theta_N^{-1}H_N^{\sigma,\mathrm{coord}}\Theta_N$ on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$. Every constant spin action commutes with the spin-independent labelled operator; a common spin unitary $A^{\otimes N}$ preserves each identical-particle sector by the finite-component lemma. For $s=0$, $M=1$ and this is the scalar product reading; for $N=1$, $M=2s+1$ and it is the one-particle component reading.

(ii) *Spatial Coulomb case.* Put $r=2s+1$, $\mathcal S_N=(\mathbb C^r)^{\otimes N}$ and $M=r^N$. Use the full spin-product unitary $\Theta_N:(L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r))^{\otimes N}\to L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$ of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]] (a),(b), including its combined spatial/internal permutation action. To apply the literal Fourier normalization of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]], choose in that mathematical theorem the masses $\widetilde m_i=m/(4\pi^2)$, its parameter $\hbar$ unchanged, one fixed center at zero, coefficients $z_{i1}=-g$ and $z_{ij}=\kappa$. The mathematical masses here are substitution parameters used to realize the already declared kinetic operator; the physical species mass remains $m$. The source kinetic symbol becomes $4\pi^2\hbar^2|\xi|^2/(2m)$, so its scalar operator is exactly
$$T_C=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta_X+V_C(X),\qquad D(T_C)=H^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C).$$
By the source's clauses (b),(c), $T_C$ and its finite-component extension are self-adjoint on these exact domains and bounded below for all stated real $g,\kappa$. The real bounded multiplier $M_{V_b}$ has norm at most $N\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b\|_\infty$, hence relative bound zero with respect to $T_C$ and to its finite-component extension. The canonical [[thm-kato-rellich]] makes
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta_X+V_C+V_b,\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})=H^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),$$
self-adjoint on exactly this domain and bounded below; if the singular operator has lower bound $c_C$, the sum has lower bound $c_C-N\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b\|_\infty$. Equal masses, identical external slots and pair-independent signed coefficient $\kappa$ make the scalar operator invariant under spatial permutations. These permutations preserve $H^2$ by permuting the weak-derivative coordinates; the constant internal tensor permutations preserve the finite-component domain too. Consequently the combined projections $\mathcal P_\sigma=\Theta_NP_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta_N^{-1}$ reduce $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, and [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]] (c) gives self-adjointness of its restriction on the exact domain $H^2\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma$. The declared sector energy is this restriction transported back by $\Theta_N^{-1}$ to $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, with the unique zero-space operator when that sector is zero. The AC assumption remains confined to this Coulomb realization as in clause (a).

(iii) *Finite-mode case.* On $K^{\otimes N}$ put
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=\sum_{i=1}^N h^{(i)}+\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}W^{(ij)},$$
where $h^{(i)}$ is the slot operator of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (the identity on all factors but
the $i$-th, $h$ on the $i$-th) and $W^{(ij)}$ is the transport of
$W\in\mathcal B(K\widehat\otimes K)$ to the pair of slots $(i,j)$ by any
canonical permutation $\pi$ whose transported map $\widehat{\pi}$ moves that pair to the first two slots; the symmetry
$U_{(0\,1)}WU_{(0\,1)}=W$ makes the order of the pair immaterial and
$W\otimes I$ commutes with permutations fixing the first two slots, so the
transported operator is independent of the permutation chosen. Then
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and self-adjoint,
it commutes with every permutation unitary, and the model's sector energy
operator is $H_N^\sigma:=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}=P_\sigma^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}P_\sigma^{(N)}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$.

**(e) The model's energy reading and evolution.** In every realization the
pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is declared to be the **assigned energy
observable** of the $N$-particle sector in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a): its
outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is the law
$\mu^{H_N^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$ of that
definition clause (b), and its spectral data are those of the self-adjoint
operator constructed in clause (d). The **model evolution** is the unitary
flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b) with this
generator. The identification of the operator with the energy of a concrete
sample, and the assignment of numerical masses, couplings and potentials to a
laboratory species, are tested identifications with uncertainty under P7;
they are not consequences of P1-P6.

**(f) The non-interacting reading.** The model is called **non-interacting**
when $W=0$ (equivalently $\kappa=0$ only in the Coulomb branch of clause (c)(ii)), so that
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$; in the spatial realization this is the
case of the external potential summed over slots of the stated bounded or Coulomb realization.

**(g) Scope.** The declared model is a kinematic and dynamical input of this
pair: it fixes a state space, a sector, an energy operator and an evolution,
and nothing else. It asserts no stability of matter, no Hunziker-van
Winter-Zhislin threshold statement, no statement about excited threshold
structure, no thermodynamic limit, no equilibration or thermalization, no
measured energy and no identification of its parameters with a particular
laboratory sample beyond the tested identifications of P7. The finite-mode
realization is an idealization confining the one-particle content to $d$
declared modes; the spatial realization is an idealization of an $N$-particle
non-relativistic sample with the declared external field and pair interaction.

**(a) Adopted readings and restricted sector class.** Adopt the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], for the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]. This definition
applies to the class of declared models whose sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is **finite-dimensional**, in particular to every
finite-mode realization
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]), where
$D:=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is finite (and may be zero) by
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a),
(b). Write $\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$ for the set of declared sector
preparations, that is, the density operators on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
If $D=0$, the only operator has trace zero, so
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)=\varnothing$. The partition trace is
$Z_N=0$, and there is no normalized canonical density or equilibrium free
energy; $\log D$, $D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ and $\log Z_N$ are not used in this
branch. Clauses (b), (d) and (e) below apply when $D\ge1$; the assigned
parameters of (c) can still be declared when $D=0$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) Dimensionless entropy.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$
with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_D\ge0$ (counted with multiplicity, in any
order), the **entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log D],$$
the quantity of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]]
clause (a) with $\log$ the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). It is dimensionless, is a function of the
eigenvalue multiset of $\rho$ alone, and equals zero exactly for pure
preparations; by clause (c) of the cited theorem $s(\rho)=\log D$ holds
exactly when $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$.

**(c) Boltzmann constant, temperature and inverse temperature.** The model
assigns a positive **Boltzmann constant** $k_B$ and a positive **temperature**
$T$; in the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the unit of $k_B$ is
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$, the unit of $T$ is the kelvin, and
$$k_B=1.380\,649\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$$
fixed exactly by the BIPM SI definition. The model declares the **inverse
temperature** $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$, a positive real number in $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
The value and exactness of $k_B$ are unit-convention facts; the assignment of
the parameter $T$ to a physical sample, and the identification of
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature, are adopted
assumptions of the ensemble model of this pair, not consequences of P1-P4,
and are tested identifications with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus postulate P7.

**(d) Physical entropy.** The **physical entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$S(\rho):=k_B\,s(\rho),$$
read in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$. It is nonnegative, is at most
$k_B\log D$, and vanishes exactly for pure preparations.

**(e) Free-energy functional.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$,
let $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)\in\mathbb R$ be the mean of the
declared energy observable in $\rho$ (finite because $D<\infty$, in the
moment reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).
The **Helmholtz free-energy reading** of $\rho$ is
$$F(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho),$$
read in joules; it is the quantity
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a)
at the identified $\beta$. For the canonical operator
$\rho_\beta:=e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}/Z_N$ and
$Z_N:=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}\in(0,\infty)$ (positive finite sum in the
nonzero finite-dimensional sector), the number $F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$
is called the **equilibrium free energy**; it is the value of the functional
at $\rho_\beta$ by the cited theorem.

**(f) Scope.** This definition covers only declared models with
finite-dimensional sector space, with the zero-sector branch of (a), and preparations in
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$. For a declared spatial realization, whose
sector space is infinite-dimensional, the operator $\rho\log\rho$ need not be
trace class; no entropy, physical entropy or free energy is defined here for
that case, and a separate trace-class statement would be required. The
definition asserts no increase of entropy in time, no equilibration to
$\rho_\beta$, no thermodynamic limit, no pressure or volume variable, and no
measured temperature, entropy or free energy.

derivations.claim: [Diagonalisation] In the basis $(|1\rangle,|2\rangle)$ the operator $h$ has the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&-t\\-t&0\end{pmatrix}$; the vectors $u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ are orthogonal unit vectors and $h u_\mp=\mp t\,u_\mp$ by direct evaluation, so $\{u_-,u_+\}$ is an orthonormal eigenbasis with eigenvalues $-t$ and $t$ by [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]. Hence $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ has the eigenvalues $0$ on $u_-$ and $2t$ on $u_+$, and it satisfies the hypothesis of [L1] with $\varepsilon=2t$, $u_0=u_-$, $u_1=u_+$. This proves (a).

[Canonical data] Applying [L1] with $\varepsilon=2t$ gives $Z=1+e^{-2\beta t}$ and $\rho_\beta=Z^{-1}(T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-2\beta t}T_{u_+,u_+})$ for $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$; since $h=(h+t\,\mathrm{id})-t\,\mathrm{id}$ and both operators are functions of the same eigenbasis, the Gibbs operator of $h$ is the same $\rho_\beta$, because the normalized Gibbs weights are unchanged by the shift: $e^{-\beta h}=e^{\beta t}e^{-\beta(h+tI)}$, so its partition trace is $Z_h=e^{\beta t}Z$ and division gives the same density. The mean of $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ is $2t/(e^{2\beta t}+1)\in(0,t)$, so $\langle h\rangle_\beta=2t/(e^{2\beta t}+1)-t=-t\tanh(\beta t)$, which lies in $(-t,0)$ because $e^{2\beta t}>1$ for $\beta t>0$; the entropy formula is that of [L1] at $\varepsilon=2t$ and satisfies $0\le s<\log2$ by [L1], and $F=-\beta^{-1}\log(1+e^{-2\beta t})-t$ is the free energy of $h$ by [L2] and [L1]. This proves (b) and (c) apart from the scope clause.

[Scope] The computation used only the declared two-dimensional model, its exact diagonalisation and the supplied two-level formulas; no physical double well, measured splitting, transition or thermodynamic limit entered, which is (d).

citations.quote:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]),
the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) and the identical-particle and
spin postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in
the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]: one-particle space
$K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with declared modes $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$,
particle number $N\ge1$, sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, one-particle
self-adjoint operator $h\in\mathcal B(K)$, and **non-interacting** interaction
$W=0$, so that $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$ and
$H_N^\sigma=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ in the notation of that
definition. Let $e_1,\dots,e_d$ be an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of
$h$ with real eigenvalues $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_d$ and let
$\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\cdots\le\varepsilon_{(d)}$ be the nondecreasing
rearrangement of the list. Then:

(a) *the labelled operator is diagonal*: $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and
self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$, it commutes with every
permutation unitary $U_\pi$, and for every multi-index
$i=(i_1,\dots,i_N)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^N$,
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}\,(e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N})=\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{i_k}\Bigr)e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N};$$

(b) *occupation eigenvalues and spectrum*: for every $N$-element subset
$J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ the Slater vector $e_J^\wedge$ of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b) is an
eigenvector of $H_N^-$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_J:=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$,
and for every occupation vector $\lambda\in W(N,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$
the symmetric vector $m_\lambda$ of clause (c) is an eigenvector of
$H_N^+$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_\lambda:=\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j\varepsilon_j$;
the families $(e_J^\wedge)$ and $(m_\lambda)$ are orthogonal bases of
$\mathfrak H_N^-$ and $\mathfrak H_N^+$ respectively, so the spectrum of
$H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of these eigenvalues (with multiplicities
given by the number of configurations producing them); for $\sigma=-$ and
$N>d$ the sector space is $\{0\}$ and the model has no sector states;

(c) *partition sum and ground energy*: write
$$\mathcal C_N^\sigma:=\{\lambda\in W(N,d):\lambda_j\le1\ \text{for every }j\ \text{if }\sigma=-\},\qquad M_N^\sigma:=|\mathcal C_N^\sigma|=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma.$$
The configuration counts are $M_N^- =\binom dN$ and
$M_N^+ =\binom{N+d-1}{N}$. For every $\beta>0$,
$$Z_N(\beta):=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$$
is finite. If $\sigma=-$ and $N>d$, then $\mathcal C_N^-=\varnothing$,
$Z_N(\beta)=0$, and there is no ground eigenvalue or trace-one density
operator on the zero sector; in particular no normalized Gibbs density can
be formed there. Otherwise $M_N^\sigma>0$ and $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$.
In this nonzero-sector case, let
$$E_0:=\min_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}\lambda_\lambda,\qquad E_{\max}:=\max_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}\lambda_\lambda.$$
Then the actual Boltzmann bounds are
$$M_N^\sigma e^{-\beta E_{\max}}\le Z_N(\beta)\le M_N^\sigma e^{-\beta E_0}.$$
No nonnegativity hypothesis on the $\varepsilon_j$ is imposed. For
$\sigma=-$ and $N\le d$,
$$E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)},\qquad E_{\max}=\sum_{k=d-N+1}^d\varepsilon_{(k)},$$
and for $\sigma=+$,
$$E_0=N\varepsilon_{(1)},\qquad E_{\max}=N\varepsilon_{(d)}.$$
For every unit vector $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in either nonzero sector,
$\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_0$, with equality exactly on the
eigenspace of $E_0$;

(d) *reading and stationarity*: on a nonzero sector the pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the
model's assigned energy observable; in a declared sector preparation $\rho$
its outcome law is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$,
and in the pure preparation of each sector basis vector of clause (b) this
law is the point mass at the displayed eigenvalue; each such vector is a
stationary state of the model evolution $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$, and
the energy law of every declared sector preparation is the law of the finite
spectral sum in the sector basis;

(e) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the finite-mode idealization, on
the declared $h$ and on $W=0$; it asserts nothing for interacting models, for
spatial realizations, for infinite mode families, about thermal states or
equilibration, and about any laboratory system.

**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). Let
$n\ge1$, and let $H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold completed tensor power with
$H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and let
$P_\pm^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$, be the permutation
projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. For a
multi-index $i=(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n$ write
$$e_i:=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\}\ (j=1,\dots,d).$$
For $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ with $|J|=n$, written $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_n\}$, put
$$e_J^\wedge:=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\, e_{j_{\widehat{\sigma}(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\widehat{\sigma}(n)}},$$
and for $\lambda\in W(n,d):=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ put
$\operatorname{orb}(\lambda):=\{c\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n:|c|=\lambda\}$ and
$m_\lambda:=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$. Then:

(a) *product basis*: $(e_i)_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}$ is an orthonormal basis of
$H^{\otimes n}$, and $\dim H^{\otimes n}=d^n$;

(b) *Slater basis*: for every $J$ with $|J|=n$ one has
$e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})$ and the
family $(e_J^\wedge)_{J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\},\ |J|=n}$ is an orthonormal family whose
closed linear span is $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$; it is therefore an
orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$,
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\binom dn$, and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$ when $n>d$. Moreover for every multi-index
$i$ one has $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=0$ when two entries of $i$ coincide, and
$$P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i)\,\frac{e_J^\wedge}{\sqrt{n!}}$$
when the entries of $i$ are pairwise distinct with underlying set $J$ and
$\rho_i\in S_n$ is the unique permutation with $i_k=j_{\widehat{\rho_i}(k)}$;

(c) *symmetric basis*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ the vector $m_\lambda$ is
nonzero, the family $(m_\lambda)_{\lambda\in W(n,d)}$ is orthogonal,
$U_\pi m_\lambda=m_\lambda$ for every $\pi\in S_n$, and for every multi-index
$i$ there is a real number $\gamma_i>0$ with
$P_+^{(n)}(e_i)=\gamma_i\,m_{|i|}$; consequently
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ is the linear span of $(m_\lambda)$, the family
$(m_\lambda)$ is an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$;

(d) *occupation operators*: for $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ the map
$$N_j:H^{\otimes n}\to H^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,e_i\rangle\,e_i,$$
is a self-adjoint bounded endomorphism, the $N_j$ commute pairwise,
$\sum_{j=1}^dN_j=nI$, and
$$N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)\,e_J^\wedge,\qquad N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_j\,m_\lambda .$$
Consequently both sectors are invariant under every $N_j$, the joint
eigenspaces of $(N_1,\dots,N_d)$ inside $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$ are the
lines $\mathbb Ce_J^\wedge$ (one for each $n$-element subset $J$, with
eigenvalue vector $\mathbf 1_J$), and the joint eigenspaces inside
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ are the lines $\mathbb Cm_\lambda$ (one for each
$\lambda\in W(n,d)$, with eigenvalue vector $\lambda$).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $H^{\otimes n}$ and
$P_\pm^{(n)}$ be as in
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] (with
$P_\pm^{(0)}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}$), and let $W(n,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$
and $m_\lambda$ be the symmetric vectors of that theorem. Then:

(a) *fermionic configurations*: the map $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ is a bijection
from the set of $n$-element subsets of $\{1,\dots,d\}$ onto the set
$\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$; consequently
$$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\#\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\textstyle\sum_j\lambda_j=n\},\qquad \sum_{n=0}^{d}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=2^{d};$$

(b) *bosonic configurations*: the assignment $\lambda\mapsto m_\lambda$ induces
a bijection from $W(n,d)$ onto the set of lines spanned by the orthogonal basis
$(m_\lambda)$, so the number of bosonic configurations of total occupation
exactly $n$ is $\binom{n+d-1}{n}=\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}$, and for every $N\ge0$ the
number of bosonic configurations of total occupation at most $N$ is
$$\sum_{n=0}^{N}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\sum_{n=0}^{N}\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}=\binom{N+d}{d};$$

(c) *exclusion counts*: no fermionic configuration has an entry $\ge2$, so the
antisymmetric Slater index set contains no $\lambda$ with $\lambda_j\ge2$ for
some $j$; for $n>d$ there is no fermionic configuration at all and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$, while for every $n$ and every $j$ the
bosonic configuration with $\lambda_j=n$ and all other entries $0$ occurs, so
no occupation bound holds in the symmetric sector;

(d) *consistency with the total occupation*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ one
has $\sum_j\lambda_j=n$, and for every fermionic configuration
$\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d\cap\{\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ likewise; in particular the
total occupation equals the particle number $n$ in both sectors.

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

derivations.claim: [Fermionic configuration sum] The two-element subsets of $\{1,2,3\}$ are $\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}$ with energies $0+\varepsilon=\varepsilon$, $0+2\varepsilon=2\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon+2\varepsilon=3\varepsilon$ by [L1]; the canonical weights are $q_J=e^{-\beta\lambda_J}/Z_{\mathrm F}$, and the occupation means are $\sum_Jq_J\mathbf 1_J(j)$ by [L2], giving the three displayed formulas. The total occupation is $\sum_Jq_J\cdot2=2$ because every configuration has two occupied modes, and the smallest energy is that of $\{1,2\}$, namely $\varepsilon$, by [L1] clause (c). This proves (a).

[Bosonic configuration sum] The occupation vectors of total two in two modes are $(2,0),(1,1),(0,2)$ with energies $0,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon$ by [L1]; the canonical weights are $q_\lambda=e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}/Z_{\mathrm B}$ and the occupation means are $\sum_\lambda q_\lambda\lambda_j$ by [L2], giving $\langle N_1\rangle=(2\cdot1+1\cdot e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+0)/Z_{\mathrm B}$ and $\langle N_2\rangle=(0+1\cdot e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+2\cdot e^{-2\beta\varepsilon})/Z_{\mathrm B}$, and the total occupation is $2$ because every configuration has $\sum_j\lambda_j=2$; the ground energy is $0=N\varepsilon_1$ by [L1] clause (c). This proves (b).

[Checks and scope] In both models $Z$ is a finite sum of positive terms, hence $0<Z<\infty$; the displayed occupation sums equal the particle number $N=2$ identically in $\beta$ by steps 1.1-1.2, and the ground energies agree with the general formulas of [L1] clause (c) for the sorted energy lists $(0,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon)$ and $(0,\varepsilon)$. Every quantity is a spectral datum of the declared finite-dimensional model; no physical species, measured occupation, thermalisation or thermodynamic limit entered, which is (c).

Adopt the canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for the mode models
declared below, the state and probability postulates P1, P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]], and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]); assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Temperatures are assigned as in
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], so that
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$. Declare the occupation readouts as assigned sharp observables $(N,1)$ and $(N_-,1)$, with unit particle-count, which is dimensionless. The total particle-number operator $\mathcal N$ in the countable-mode reading has the same unit; every occupation mean and higher number moment below is read in the corresponding dimensionless count unit. Then:

(a) *single bosonic mode*: let $F(\mathbb C)$ be the one-mode Fock space with
number operator $N$ and orthonormal number basis $(e_n)$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]]), let
$\varepsilon>0$ and let the model declare the energy operator $H:=\varepsilon N$
on $F(\mathbb C)$; the model's canonical preparation at temperature $T$ is
$\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z$ with $Z=(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$, the
number readout $N$ is an assigned sharp observable with finite thermal mean
$$\langle N\rangle_\beta=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}=\frac1{e^{\varepsilon/(k_BT)}-1},$$
and all moments $\langle N^k\rangle_\beta$, $k\ge1$, are finite;

(b) *single fermionic orbital and grand-canonical shift*: on
$\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^2$ with occupation operator $N_-$ and
$\varepsilon_1,\mu\in\mathbb R$, the model's canonical (grand-canonical)
preparation $F=Z^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^1e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}T_{u_k,u_k}$
has $Z=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}$, $\operatorname{tr}F=1$, and occupation mean
$$\langle N_-\rangle=\frac1{e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1};$$
the same formula is the model's thermal mean when $\mu=0$ and
$\varepsilon_1>0$;

(c) *countably many independent modes*: let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$
and $\mu\in\mathbb R$, and let the model declare the free-mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ (one mode case of clause (a)) with the product reading of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]; then the
bosonic product partition is finite exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$ and $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j$, and
the fermionic product partition is finite exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$; in the finite cases the products
equal $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)})^{-1}$ and
$\prod_j(1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)})$ respectively;

(d) *dilute remainders*: for $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)}$ the model's
occupation means satisfy the exact identities
$$\frac q{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q}\quad(\text{bosonic},\ 0<q<1),\qquad \frac q{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q}\quad(\text{fermionic},\ q>0),$$
so both differ from $q$ by at most $q^2/(1-q)$ and $q^2/(1+q)$
respectively;

(e) *scope*: clauses (a)-(d) are conditional statements about the declared
mode models together with the adopted ensemble assignment; they assert no
thermodynamic limit, no continuum of radiation modes, no Bose-Einstein
condensation, no measured occupation number, and no thermalisation of a
sample. All numerical equalities are exact identities of the declared
finite-mode (or product) models at the assigned temperature.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\beta>0$ and let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$ and
$\mu\in\mathbb R$ be real data; write $q_j:=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)}$.

(a) *Single fermionic orbital.* On $\mathfrak h:=\mathbb C^2$ with orthonormal
basis $(u_0,u_1)$ define the bounded self-adjoint operator $N_-$ by
$N_-u_0=0$, $N_-u_1=u_1$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Then the diagonal
operator $F:=\sum_{k=0}^1e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}\,T_{u_k,u_k}$ is
positive, self-adjoint, finite rank, and
$$\operatorname{tr}F=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)},\qquad \frac{\sum_{k=0}^1k\,e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}}{\operatorname{tr}F}=\frac1{e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1}$$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]],
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(b) *Countable grand-canonical factor products.* Define
$\mathcal N:=\{N\subseteq\{1,2,\dots\}:N\text{ finite}\}$ and set
$$Z_{\mathrm B}:=\sup_{N\in\mathcal N}\ \prod_{j\in N}\frac1{1-q_j}\in(0,\infty],\qquad Z_{\mathrm F}:=\sup_{N\in\mathcal N}\ \prod_{j\in N}(1+q_j)\in[1,\infty],$$
with the convention $Z_{\mathrm B}:=+\infty$ if some $j$ has
$\varepsilon_j-\mu\le0$. Then:
$$Z_{\mathrm B}<\infty\iff\sum_j e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty \ \text{ and }\ \mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j,\qquad Z_{\mathrm F}<\infty\iff\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty,$$
and in these finite cases $Z_{\mathrm B}=\prod_{j\ge1}(1-q_j)^{-1}$ and
$Z_{\mathrm F}=\prod_{j\ge1}(1+q_j)$.

(c) *Mode occupancies and dilute remainders.* For a single mode with
$0<q<1$ (boson) and $q>0$ (fermion),
$$\frac{\sum_{n\ge0}n\,q^n}{\sum_{n\ge0}q^n}=\frac q{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q},\qquad \frac{\sum_{n=0}^1n\,q^n}{\sum_{n=0}^1q^n}=\frac q{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q};$$
consequently the deviations from $q$ are bounded by $q^2/(1-q)$ and
$q^2/(1+q)$ respectively, and both are at most $2q^2$ when $q\le1/2$.

All statements are mathematical statements about diagonal weights and products;
no identification of $\beta,\mu,\varepsilon_j$ with physical temperatures,
chemical potentials or energies, and no thermal or thermodynamic conclusion,
is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with a countable complete orthonormal family $(e_j)_{j\ge1}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$, let $\beta>0$, and let
$F(H)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]. Let
$\mathcal M$ be the set of finite nondecreasing sequences
$I=(j_1\le\cdots\le j_n)$ with $n\ge0$ (the empty sequence included); for
$I=(j_1\le\cdots\le j_n)$ put
$$v_I:=P_+^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})\in F(H)\quad(n\ge1),\qquad v_{\varnothing}:=\Omega,\qquad \lambda_I:=\varepsilon_{j_1}+\cdots+\varepsilon_{j_n}\ (\text{empty sum }0),$$
and $u_I:=v_I/\|v_I\|$. Then:

(a) $(u_I)_{I\in\mathcal M}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(H)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]);

(b) the diagonal operator
$$D(D_\beta):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-2\beta\lambda_I}|\langle\psi,u_I\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad D_\beta\psi:=\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}\langle\psi,u_I\rangle u_I$$
is bounded, self-adjoint and positive with $\|D_\beta\|\le1$; it is trace class
exactly when $\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}<\infty$, and then
$\operatorname{tr}D_\beta=\sum_Ie^{-\beta\lambda_I}$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);

(c) for every $N\ge1$, $\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{I\in\mathcal M\\ I\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}}}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\prod_{j=1}^N\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}$, and
$$\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\lim_{N\to\infty}\prod_{j=1}^N\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}\in(0,\infty];$$

(d) *product criterion*: $\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}<\infty$ if and only if
$\sum_{j\ge1}e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$, and in that case
$$\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\prod_{j=1}^\infty\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}<\infty ;$$

(e) consequently $D_\beta$ is trace class if and only if
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$, with the trace given by the infinite
product in (d).

The operator $D_\beta$ is a purely mathematical diagonal operator on $F(H)$;
no thermal, thermodynamic or measurement interpretation is asserted.

Let $r \in \mathbb{R}$ and let $r^k$ be the integer power ([[def-integer-power]]),
so that $r^0 = 1$ for every $r$, including $r = 0$.

1. If $|r| < 1$ then the series $\sum r^k$ converges ([[def-series]]) and
   $$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} r^{k} \;=\; \frac{1}{1-r} .$$
2. If $|r| \ge 1$ then $\sum r^k$ diverges.

The series starts at $k = 0$ and its first term is $r^0 = 1$; in particular
$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} 2^{-k} = 2$, while the series starting at $k = 1$ sums to
$1$. Which starting index is meant has to be said, and it is said here.

derivations.claim: [Dilute identities] In the canonical reading, $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(0,1)$; in the grand-canonical reading, $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)}>0$, with the bosonic formula restricted to $\mu<\varepsilon$ and hence $q<1$. By [L1], the bosonic and fermionic means on these respective domains are $q/(1-q)$ and $q/(1+q)$. The algebraic identities $q/(1-q)=q+q^2/(1-q)$ for $0<q<1$ and $q/(1+q)=q-q^2/(1+q)$ for $q>0$ are exact; the bosonic correction is positive and the fermionic correction is negative, with absolute values $q^2/(1-q)$ and $q^2/(1+q)$. This proves (a).

[The two convergence examples] For $\varepsilon_j=j\varepsilon$ the sum is $\sum_{j\ge1}(e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})<\infty$ by [L2], and for the bosonic product one needs in addition $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j=\varepsilon$; for $\varepsilon_j\equiv\varepsilon$ every term of the sum equals $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}>0$, so the sum diverges and [L2] makes both product partitions infinite. This proves (c).

[Checks and scope] Steps 1.1-1.3 give the exact identities, the exact rational check, and the two convergence outcomes; every quantity is computed in the declared mode models at the assigned temperature, and no measured occupation, dilute gas, thermodynamic limit or condensation entered, which is (d).

citations.quote:
**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P4 together with P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P4, P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics, assert no dynamics for a prescribed time-dependent family or for an open system (clauses (iv) and (v) of P4 are separate model assumptions treated on their own pages), assert no measurement model, no apparatus realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any laboratory system is exactly isolated.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space
([[def-measurable-space]], [[def-sigma-algebra]]) and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on
$(X,\Sigma)$ is a map

$$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$

such that:

1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a
   bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional
   restriction;
2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$;
3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$;
4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with
   union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm
   to $E(B)x$, that is
   $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$

Clause 4 is **strong countable additivity**. A PVM is called **regular** when
$X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), the
$\sigma$-algebra is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and every one of the finite
positive measures

$$E_x(B):=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,\qquad x\in H,\ B\in\Sigma,$$

is a regular Borel measure ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]). Inner
products are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); this fixed convention is the one
used for every pairing $E_{x,y}(B)=\langle E(B)x,y\rangle$ on this page.

**Well-definedness: the projection clause.** The conditions $P^2=P=P^*$ are
simultaneously meaningful and describe exactly the Hilbert orthogonal
projections, with no hidden finite-dimensional hypothesis. Indeed, for a
bounded $P$ with $P^2=P=P^*$ the range $\operatorname{ran}P$ is a linear
subspace, and for $y=Pw$ one has
$\langle x-Px,y\rangle=\langle P(x-Px),w\rangle=\langle Px-P^2x,w\rangle=0$, so
$x-Px\perp\operatorname{ran}P$; conversely $\langle Pz,Pz\rangle=\langle z,P^*Pz\rangle=\langle z,Pz\rangle=0$
for $z\perp\operatorname{ran}P$, so $z\in\ker P$, while
$\langle z,Px\rangle=\langle Pz,x\rangle=0$ for $z\in\ker P$ gives
$\ker P=(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$
([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Hence
$\operatorname{ran}P=(\ker P)^\perp$ is closed, and the two defining properties
$Px\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $x-Px\in(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ of
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]] show that $P=P_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is
the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace, and conversely every
such $P_M$ is idempotent and self-adjoint by
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]] and
[[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]. Finally $P$ is
contractive: from $\langle Px,x\rangle=\langle Px,Px\rangle=\|Px\|^2$ and
Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|Px\|^2\le\|Px\|\,\|x\|$, so $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ for all $x$,
and $\langle Px,x\rangle=\|Px\|^2\ge0$ is a nonnegative real number.

**Well-definedness: the regularity clause.** For an orthogonal projection value
the pairing $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a nonnegative real number and
$E_x(X)=\langle x,x\rangle=\|x\|^2<+\infty$, so every $E_x$ is a finite
nonnegative set function and the regularity requirement is a meaningful
condition on it; that each $E_x$ is genuinely a countably additive measure of
total mass $\|x\|^2$, and that the polarized pairings $E_{x,y}$ are finite
complex measures, is proved as
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(-x)=-\sin x,\qquad\cos(-x)=\cos x,\qquad\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1.$$
Consequently $|\sin x|\le1$ and $|\cos x|\le1$.

Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P7 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], and work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with:
one-particle space $K=\mathbb C^2$, declared sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$ an
orthonormal basis of $K$, particle number $N=1$, single site-occupation
sector, and the declared one-particle operator (the **bond Hamiltonian**)
$$h:=-t\bigl(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle}\bigr),\qquad t>0\ \text{in joules}.$$
Adopt the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ and inverse temperature $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, and read
$\varepsilon:=2t$ as the tunnelling splitting. Then:

(a) $h$ has the orthonormal eigenbasis
$$u_-:=\frac{|1\rangle+|2\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad u_+:=\frac{|1\rangle-|2\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad h u_\mp=\mp t\,u_\mp,$$
so its eigenvalues are $-t$ and $+t$; equivalently $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ is the
two-level Hamiltonian of
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-two-level-thermal-formulas]] with levels $0$ and
$\varepsilon=2t$ and eigenvectors $u_-,u_+$;

(b) the canonical preparation of $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ and hence of $h$ is
$$\rho_\beta=\frac{T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-2\beta t}\,T_{u_+,u_+}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},$$
with shifted partition sum $Z_0=1+e^{-2\beta t}$ and physical partition trace $Z_h=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta h}=e^{\beta t}Z_0$;

(c) the exact means, entropy and free energy are
$$\langle h\rangle_\beta=\frac{2t}{e^{2\beta t}+1}-t=-t\tanh(\beta t),\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)+\frac{2\beta te^{-2\beta t}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},\qquad F=-\frac1\beta\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)-t,$$
and for every $\beta>0$ one has $-t<\langle h\rangle_\beta<0$ and
$0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log2$;

(d) *scope*: the computation is an exact statement about the declared
two-dimensional bond model at the assigned temperature; it identifies no
physical double-well or molecular system, asserts no measured splitting and
no transition, and the temperature assignment is the tested identification of
P7.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\varepsilon>0$ and $\beta>0$ be real parameters, let $\mathfrak h$ be a
two-dimensional complex Hilbert space with orthonormal basis
$(u_0,u_1)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and let $H:=T_{u_1,u_1}\varepsilon=\varepsilon\,T_{u_1,u_1}$ be the
self-adjoint operator with eigenvalues $0$ on $\mathbb Cu_0$ and
$\varepsilon$ on $\mathbb Cu_1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). Let
$$Z:=\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j},\qquad \rho_\beta:=\frac1Z\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j}T_{u_j,u_j},\qquad s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i$$
be the partition sum, canonical operator and entropy of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause
(a), with $E_0=0$, $E_1=\varepsilon$ and $w_i$ the eigenvalues of a density
operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak h$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]]). Then:

(a) $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(1,2)$, and
$$\rho_\beta=\frac1Z\bigl(T_{u_0,u_0}+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}T_{u_1,u_1}\bigr)$$
is a density operator on $\mathfrak h$ that is not the maximally mixed state
$\tfrac12\mathrm{id}$;

(b) the mean energy is the exact identity
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\frac{\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{Z}=\frac{\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1},\qquad 0<\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2};$$

(c) the entropy and free energy satisfy
$$s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z+\frac{\beta\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}=\log\bigl(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\bigr)+\frac{\beta\varepsilon\,e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}},\qquad 0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log 2,$$
and, with $F:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=F ;$$

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) are exact algebraic identities for the
declared two-dimensional Hilbert space and the two real parameters
$\varepsilon,\beta>0$; no temperature, thermodynamic, equilibrium or
measurement interpretation is asserted, and the parameter $\beta$ carries no
physical dimension in this lemma.

Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], the state postulate P1
and the observable postulate P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], and adopt the
canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for the canonical
preparation $\rho_\beta$; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in the
finite-sector class of the entropy definition: the declared model has
finite-dimensional sector space $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, self-adjoint energy
operator $H_N^\sigma$ with flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$, and every declared sector preparation
evolves as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^*$ under P4 clause (iii). Then:

(a) *entropy is conserved*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho(0)$
of the model and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$s(\rho(t))=s(\rho(0));$$

(b) *the canonical preparation is stationary*:
$U(t)\rho_\beta U(t)^*=\rho_\beta$ for every $t$, and every thermal mean
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)$ of an assigned observable is time
independent;

(c) *no unitary production of the canonical preparation*: if
$\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$ then $\rho(t)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;
equivalently, no evolution of this isolated model maps a non-canonical
declared preparation to the canonical one at any time;

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) concern the model's exact unitary flow in the
finite-sector class and the adopted canonical preparation. They assert
nothing about open systems or environment coupling, about the time behaviour
of individual readouts or their time averages, about an approach of any
readout to a thermal value in a limit, about environments or measurement
models, and about any laboratory sample; in particular clause (c) is not a
claim that no physical system ever approaches thermal equilibrium, but the
statement that the model's P4 dynamics alone does not do so.

derivations.claim: [The evolved preparation and the site readout] With $\psi_0=|1\rangle=(u_-+u_+)/\sqrt2$, [F1] gives $\psi(\tau)=U(\tau)\psi_0=(e^{i\theta}u_-+e^{-i\theta}u_+)/\sqrt2$, where $\theta:=t\tau/\hbar$; by [F2] and $u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ this equals $\cos\theta\,|1\rangle+i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, a unit vector. Since $T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}=\tfrac12(I+\sigma_z)$ with $\sigma_z=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}-T_{|2\rangle,|2\rangle}$, and $\sigma_z\psi(\tau)=\cos\theta\,|1\rangle-i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, the site-occupation mean is $\langle P_1\rangle(\tau)=|\cos\theta|^2=\cos^2\theta=\cos^2(t\tau/\hbar)$, in particular $\langle P_1\rangle(0)=1$.

[Canonical means and the initial comparison] By [F3], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta h)=-t\tanh(\beta t)<0$; moreover $\rho_\beta$ is diagonal in the basis $(u_-,u_+)$ with strictly positive diagonal weights, so $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta\sigma_z)=0$ because $\sigma_z$ exchanges the two basis vectors, and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta P_1)=\tfrac12$; and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(0)P_1)=1\ne\tfrac12$, so $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$.

[The preparation is never canonical] Step 1.2 shows $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$; applying [F4] to the declared finite-sector model gives $\rho(\tau)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$, which is (a).

[The energy readout never takes its thermal value] Since $h$ commutes with $U(\tau)$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\tau)h)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(0)h)=\langle h\Psi,\Psi\rangle$ for $\Psi:=|1\rangle$, and this vanishes because $h\Psi=-t|2\rangle$ is orthogonal to $\Psi$; by step 1.2 the canonical mean is $-t\tanh(\beta t)<0$, so the two values never agree. This proves (c), and step 1.1 proves (b) together with the comparison of step 1.2.

[Conclusion and scope] Steps 2.1-2.2 prove (a)-(c) for the declared hypothetical preparation. The scenario is an exact model deduction from the declared preparation, the bond Hamiltonian and the canonical data; no observed equilibration, measured readout or laboratory system entered, which is (d).
